« Un trait de vin » = a splash of wine; also a line or a feature.
Reflexive infinitive: « qu'on laisse s'évaporer » = which one lets boil away.
The year Timor-Leste became independent, on 20 May 2002; « le Timor-Leste naît en 2002 » = Timor-Leste is born in 2002.
« Son vieil ennemi » = its old enemy; feminine « ennemie ».
French writes the decimal with a comma: « 1,3 million d'habitants » = 1.3 million people.
« Le pays n'a pas attendu de miracle » = the country did not wait for a miracle; after a negation « un » becomes « de ».
Past participle of libérer, used in the passive: « un ovule est libéré » = an egg is released.
The year the fifteen-year-old Ramanujan borrowed the book; « nous sommes en 1903 » = it is 1903.
The year Arunachalam Muruganantham saw his wife hiding a rag; « en 1998 » = in 1998.
The first name of Arunachalam Muruganantham, the Indian inventor of a low-cost pad machine; « la femme d'Arunachalam » = Arunachalam's wife.
Arunachalam Muruganantham (born 1962), from Coimbatore in southern India, who tested his cheap pads on himself; India honoured him with the Padma Shri in 2016.
« Cacher un chiffon » = to hide a rag; a piece of old cloth.
« Les serviettes hygiéniques » = sanitary pads; the h is silent.
Plural of « roupie », the currency of India: « pour quelques roupies » = for a few rupees.
The year India gave Muruganantham one of its highest civilian honours.
Plural of « entreprise » (company, business): « pas à des entreprises » = not to companies.
An English word used in French, pronounced « scouteur »; « un scooter ».
The year Brian May began his doctorate at Imperial College, London.
The first name of Brian May, guitarist of Queen and astrophysicist.
« Étudier la physique » = to study physics; as an adjective, « physique » means physical.
« Commencer un doctorat sur… » = to begin a doctorate on…
« La poussière de l'espace », « la poussière entre les planètes » = the dust between the planets.
« Jouer de la guitare » = to play the guitar: instruments take « de ».
The British rock band founded in London in 1970, in which Brian May plays guitar.
Present of gagner: « la musique gagne » = the music wins; also means to earn.
The year Brian May finished his doctorate, thirty-seven years after starting it.
Numbers from 17 to 99 are hyphenated: « trente-sept ans de retard » = thirty-seven years late.
« La thèse s'est arrêtée » = the thesis stopped; the written work of a doctorate.
« Dans le bois d'une vieille cheminée » = from the wood of an old fireplace; also means chimney.
« Platon avait vu ce lien » = Plato had seen the link; from lier, to tie.
« Musical » (masculine), « musicale » (feminine): « un temps musical » = a musical beat, « l'éducation musicale » = musical training.
« L'Imperial College », the London university where Brian May studied physics; « l' » = le before a vowel.
The English word in the name « Imperial College », kept in English; the French « collège » is a secondary school.
The year Pellegrino Artusi printed his cookbook himself; « en 1891 » = in 1891.
The first name of Pellegrino Artusi.
Pellegrino Artusi (1820–1911), a retired merchant whose self-published cookbook of 1891 holds the first written recipe for the sauce of Bologna; « le livre d'Artusi » = Artusi's book.
Plural of « éditeur »; « les éditeurs disent non » = the publishers say no.
« Soixante et onze » = seventy-one: French counts 60 + 11, with « et » and no hyphen.
Forms of imprimer: « il l'imprime » present with « l' » (the book), « a imprimé » passé composé, « faire imprimer » = to have printed, « imprimée » agreeing with « la recette ».
« Un commerçant à la retraite » = a retired merchant; feminine « commerçante ».
Plural of « édition »: « quatorze éditions » = fourteen editions.
« De son vivant » = in his lifetime, while he was alive; from vivre.
« À la retraite » = retired; « prendre sa retraite » = to retire.
« Tous les éditeurs d'Italie » = every publisher in Italy; « l'Italie » = Italy.
Timor-Leste (also « le Timor oriental »), the country in South-East Asia that became independent on 20 May 2002; masculine: « le Timor-Leste », « au Timor-Leste ».
« La douleur s'arrête » = the pain stops; « faire mal » says the same thing with a verb.
Forms of soigner: « des antibiotiques soignent l'infection » present, « ont soigné » passé composé.
Present of s'assombrir (from « sombre », dark): « le monde s'assombrit peu à peu » = the world slowly goes dark.
Present of s'obscurcir; « le monde s'obscurcit par degrés » = the world dims by degrees.
Plural of « degré »; « par degrés » = by degrees, little by little.
Imparfait of redouter (to dread), third person plural: « les villages le redoutaient » = the villages dreaded it.
Passé simple of employer: « il employa quatre outils » = it used four tools; « employé » is also a noun, a clerk.
« Que » + « avec » with elision, in « ne … que » (only): « il n'était heureux qu'avec les nombres » = he was happy only with numbers.
Plural of « calcul »: « calculs le jour, mathématiques la nuit » = sums by day, mathematics by night.
The mathematical word for a proof: « sans une seule démonstration » = without a single proof; « preuve » is the everyday word.
Imparfait of figurer (to appear, be listed): « qui ne figuraient nulle part dans le livre » = that were nowhere in the book.
Inverted imparfait of falloir after « encore »: « encore fallait-il manger » = still, one had to eat.
french.translation: was it necessary, one had to

french.note: « L'angoisse » = la angoisse, a deep, anxious fear: « dans l'angoisse » = in dread.
Same form for both genders: « des années de travail solitaire » = years of work alone.
Past participle of ronger used as an adjective: « rongé par le mal du pays » = eaten up by homesickness.
Passé simple of ruiner: « le froid ruina sa santé » = the cold broke his health.
« Un cycle dure 28 jours » = a cycle lasts 28 days.
Plural of « crampe »; « des crampes » are the aching pains of the period.
« La fatigue » = tiredness; the adjective is « fatigué(e) ».
« L'envie » (a wish, a longing) with « de » elided: « trois à sept jours de crampes et d'envie de repos » = of cramps and a wish to rest.
« L'envie de repos » = a wish to rest; « repos » ends in a silent s even in the singular.
Plural of « hormone », feminine in French: « les hormones baissent » in the last week of the cycle.
Plural of « larme »: « larmes sans raison », « larmes venues de nulle part » = tears from nowhere.
Past participle of honorer: « l'Inde l'a honoré » = India honoured him; with avoir, it agrees only with a direct object before it (« l' » = him).
Present of se reformer: « la muqueuse se reforme » = the lining grows back.
« L'irritabilité » = being easily annoyed; one of the feelings of the last week of the cycle.
« Du sang animal » = animal blood; the adjective follows the noun.
Past participle of humilier, feminine to agree with « sa femme »: « sa femme, humiliée, le quitta ».
Present of s'éliminer; « la muqueuse de l'utérus s'élimine » = the lining of the womb is shed — a reflexive verb doing the work of a passive.
Present of se reconstituer: « la muqueuse se reconstitue » = the lining regrows.
Present of chuter, third person plural: « les hormones chutent » = the hormones fall sharply; stronger than « baissent ».
Passé simple of persévérer: « il persévéra jusqu'à ce que… » = he kept going until…
Passé simple of décerner, used for prizes and honours: « l'Inde lui décerna une haute distinction ».
« Une haute distinction » = a high honour (the Padma Shri, given in 2016).
Short for « Jésus-Christ »: « avant J.-C. » = BC, « vers 375 avant J.-C. » = around 375 BC.
« C'est une joie » = it is a joy.
« Sur scène » = on stage, without an article; « une scène » is also a scene.
« In- » + « achevé » (finished): « un peu inachevé à l'intérieur », « une petite chose inachevée ».
Passé simple of entamer (to begin, cut into): « il entama un doctorat » = he began a doctorate.
« La poussière interplanétaire » = the dust between the planets.
Passé simple of s'interrompre: « la thèse s'interrompit » = the thesis stopped.
Plural of « maître »: « le plus puissant des maîtres » = the most powerful of teachers.
Feminine of « content », agreeing with « la famille »: « la famille est contente ».
« L'attente » = la attente, the noun of attendre: « l'attente est le moment difficile » = the waiting is the hard part.
Present of débattre (de), third person plural: « celle dont les cuisiniers débattent encore » = the one cooks still argue about.
Present of blesser (to wound): « ce qui, à soixante et onze ans, blesse » = which at seventy-one stings.
Present of embaumer: « leur odeur embaume la maison » = their smell fills the house.
The year of the last human rabies death in Chile.
A deadly virus passed on by animal bites; « la rage » always takes the article.
« Un chien » = a dog; « à cause d'un chien » = because of a dog.
Plural of « chat » (cat); « les chiens et les chats » = dogs and cats.
The country in South America; written « le Chili » in French, with the article.
The continent; « en Asie » = in Asia, with « en » before a feminine continent.
The US capital, where the WHO's regional office for the Americas sits.
The Swiss city where the World Health Organization has its headquarters.
A document that proves something officially.
Past participle of certifier; « a certifié » is the passé composé, « the WHO has certified ».
« La morsure d'un chien » = a dog's bite; the plural adds -s.
Present and past participle of vacciner: « Le Chili vaccine ses chiens »; « a vacciné » is the passé composé.
Workers who give vaccinations; the plural adds -s.
The act of vaccinating; nouns in -tion are feminine in French.
A hyphenated compound: demi- (half) + siècle (century); « un demi-siècle » = fifty years.
Same form for masculine and feminine: « le résultat était invisible ».
An ancient disease that the WHO also validated as eliminated in Chile in 2026.
Feminine of « mortel », agreeing with « rage ».
Plural of « symptôme », a sign of a disease.
Past participle of valider used as an adjective: « validé pour l'élimination » = validated for the elimination.
Nouns in -tion are feminine; « l'élimination » is « la » shortened before a vowel.
Masculine; the -s is the same in singular and plural.
A hyphenated token: là (there) + bas (down); « personne là-bas » = nobody there.
Same word as in English, with a French pronunciation.
Close and constant watching; a feminine noun.
Feminine of « constant », agreeing with « surveillance ».
Past participle of contracter used as an adjective: « la rage contractée » = rabies caught; it agrees with « rage ».
A literary word for « autrefois »: « jadis la peur » = fear in the old days.
Contraction of « de » + « étrange »: « ce qu'il y a d'étrange » = what is strange.
« L'exploit » is « le exploit » shortened before a vowel; masculine.
The day of the month: « le 4 octobre » is read « le quatre octobre », with no word for « of ».
« La Formule 1 » is read « Formule un ».
The year of the last Formula 1 race at Sepang before this one; read « deux mille dix-sept ».
90 in the French of France, literally « four twenties and ten »; a hyphenated single word.
French writes decimals with a comma: « 2,3 secondes » is read « deux virgule trois secondes ».
Read « quatre-vingt-quatre », literally four twenties and four.
Months take no capital letter: « le dimanche 4 octobre 2026 ».
The place in Malaysia where the race circuit is; « à Sepang » = at Sepang.
A country in Asia; it is feminine, so « en Malaisie » = in Malaysia.
Max Verstappen, the Red Bull driver who wins this race.
The Formula 1 team Max Verstappen drives for; the two English words stay unchanged in French.
A Formula 1 team; after a noun the name stays unchanged: « les deux pilotes Mercedes ».
First name of the Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli.
Kimi Antonelli, a Mercedes driver, second in this race and first in the championship; « d'Antonelli » = of Antonelli, with « de » shortened before the vowel.
George Russell, the other Mercedes driver, whose car stops near the end.
First name of the Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton.
Lewis Hamilton, the Ferrari driver who finishes third in this race.
The Formula 1 team Lewis Hamilton drives for.
The city where the next race is; it takes no article: « à Singapour ».
A country in the Gulf that gives this Grand Prix its name; used without an article: « le Grand Prix de Bahreïn ».
Present of pleuvoir, used only with « il »: « il pleut » = it rains.
The noun of partir: « au départ » = at the start (of the race).
« Sa première victoire » = his first win; same family as English « victory ».
The closed road where races are run: « ce circuit » = this track.
Past participle of reprendre (re- + prendre): « il a repris la première place » = he took first place again.
From « champion »; « mener le championnat » = to lead the championship.
Past participle of déplacer (to move) used as an adjective or in the passive: « avait été déplacé » = had been moved.
Borrowed from English: « la pole position », or just « la pole », is the first place at the start; « en pole » = on pole.
Nouns in -tion are feminine; « partir en pole position » = to start from pole position.
Feminine of « mouillé », agreeing with « piste ».
Forms of doubler, which means to overtake on a road or a track as well as to double: passé simple « il doubla », « ils doublèrent »; past participle « doublés », with -s after « les ».
Feminine of « torrentiel », from « torrent »: « une pluie torrentielle » = very heavy rain.
From « patient »; « faire patienter quelqu'un » = to keep someone waiting.
Stronger than « mouillée »: full of water; it agrees with « piste ».
Passé simple of s'élancer, to set off with speed: « il s'élança lentement » = he got away slowly.
Past participle of regrouper (re- + grouper); « eut regroupé » is the passé antérieur, « had bunched up ».
The group of competitors in a race: « regrouper le peloton » = to bunch the field up.
Passé simple of remonter (re- + monter): « il remonta jusqu'à la troisième place » = he climbed back to third place.
« L'avance » is « la avance » shortened before a vowel: the gap between the leader and the next one; « 84 points d'avance » = a lead of 84 points.
Past participle of monter; with être it agrees with the subject: « l'avance est montée à 84 points ».
Always « quant à »: « quant à Verstappen » = as for Verstappen; not to be confused with « quand » (when).
The year the story begins, when nobody in Billund was ordering a house; « nous sommes en 1932 » = it is 1932.
The year Ole's workshop burned down for the first time.
The year Ole's workshop burned down for the second time.
The year the wooden duck joined Ole's toys; « dès 1935 » = from 1935 on.
The year Ole named his company LEGO; « en 1934 » = in 1934.
The year the plastic brick was patented, on 28 January, and the year Ole died, on 11 March.
The day in « le 11 mars », read « le onze mars »; French puts the day before the month.
The village in Denmark where Ole Kirk Christiansen had his workshop.
The country of the story; it is masculine, so « au Danemark » = in Denmark and « du Danemark » = of Denmark.
The first name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the carpenter of this story; « d'Ole » = de + Ole, shortened before the vowel.
The middle part of the full name Ole Kirk Christiansen.
The family name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter who made wooden toys.
Ole's son, who had to varnish every duck again that night.
The name Ole gave his company in 1934, from the Danish words for « joue bien » (play well); written in capitals.
A person who builds the wooden parts of houses; after « être », a profession takes no article: « Ole est charpentier ».
Ne + achète (present of acheter), shortened before the vowel: « personne n'achète de maison » = nobody buys a house.
From « jouer » (to play); « des jouets en bois » = wooden toys.
A hyphenated word; the plural adds -s at the end only: « des yo-yos ».
« Un canard en bois » = a wooden duck; the final -d is silent.
Present of vernir, third person singular: « son fils vernit les canards » = his son varnishes the ducks.
Forms of reconstruire (re- + construire): « reconstruit » is the present and the past participle (« il l'a reconstruit »), « reconstruisit » the passé simple.
Forms of commander (to order something from a maker): « a commandé » is the passé composé, « commandait » the imparfait.
Plural of « roulette », a little wheel: « un canard à roulettes » = a duck on wheels.
The clear liquid that protects and shines wood; the final -s is there in the singular too: « le vernis ».
Past participle of renvoyer (re- + envoyer): « Ole l'a renvoyé » = Ole sent him back.
Re- + vernir: to varnish a second time; « a reverni » is the passé composé, « revernir » the infinitive.
Of Denmark: « le village danois », « des mots danois »; nationalities take no capital letter as adjectives.
Past participle of économiser: « il avait économisé de l'argent » = he had saved money.
Reflexive « s'offrir quelque chose » = to buy oneself something; « ne rien pouvoir s'offrir d'autre » = to be able to afford nothing else.
french.translation: to afford, to treat oneself to

french.note: Present participle of espérer: « espérant faire des économies » = hoping to save money.
Usually plural: « faire des économies » = to save money.
Passé simple of expédier, to send goods off: « il expédia un lot de canards ».
A number of goods made or sent together: « un lot de canards » = a batch of ducks.
A short sentence that says what a person or a company stands for: « la devise de l'entreprise ».
A small block for building; here a toy brick: « sa brique en plastique ».
Past participle of breveter, to protect an invention by a patent (un brevet): « la brique fut brevetée » is a passive, agreeing with « brique ».
The third month; months take no capital letter, and the final -s is pronounced: « le 11 mars ».
The year the story begins, when Lucy Wills is in Bombay; « nous sommes en 1928 » = it is 1928.
The city in India where Lucy Wills worked in 1928; « à Bombay » = in Bombay, with « à » before a city.
The first name of Lucy Wills, the English doctor of this story.
The family name of Lucy Wills; « le facteur de Wills » = the Wills factor, the first name given to folic acid.
Said of a woman who is expecting a baby: « une femme enceinte », plural « des femmes enceintes ».
Plural of « pâle », with little colour in the face; the same form for masculine and feminine.
A place where workers make things with machines; « travailler en usine » = to work in a factory.
Question form of « elles mangent » (manger, to eat): verb, hyphen, pronoun; « que mangent-elles ? » = what do they eat?
« À tartiner » after a food means made for spreading: « de la levure à tartiner » = yeast spread, like « du fromage à tartiner ».
A substance in food that the body needs in small amounts; feminine in French: « la vitamine ».
« L'acide folique » = folic acid; « l'acide » is le + acide and « d'acide » is de + acide, both shortened before the vowel.
Used in « l'acide folique » = folic acid, the vitamin of this story; the same form for masculine and feminine.
Imperative of demander for « vous »; the person you ask takes « à »: « demandez à votre médecin » = ask your doctor.
The year Lucy Wills wrote down and published what she had found.
Read « quatre cents »; « 400 microgrammes d'acide folique » is the daily amount in the advice.
Plural of « une ouvrière », a woman who works with her hands in a factory; the masculine is « un ouvrier ».
As a noun « le textile » is the whole cloth industry: « les ouvrières du textile » = the women who work in the textile factories.
Plural of « un rat »; the final -t and -s are silent.
Irregular plural of « un animal »: nouns in -al usually take -aux.
Plural of « un microgramme », one millionth of a gram: « 400 microgrammes d'acide folique » = 400 micrograms of folic acid.
Present of réduire, third person singular: « cela réduit le risque » = it lowers the risk; it makes the risk smaller, it does not remove it.
The chance that something bad happens; « le risque de problèmes » = the risk of problems.
« La colonne vertébrale » = the spine, the column of bones in the back.
Feminine of « vertébral »; used in « la colonne vertébrale » = the spine, the backbone.
The year the substance was found in spinach and named folic acid; « jusqu'en 1941 » = until 1941.
The illness of this story, which left the women pale and exhausted; feminine: « une anémie dangereuse ».
Forms of soupçonner, to think that something is the cause: « soupçonnait » is the imparfait (she suspected), « soupçonnant » the present participle (suspecting).
Plural of « anémique », ill with anaemia: « ils sont devenus anémiques » = they became anaemic.
Past participle of guérir: « a guéri les femmes » = cured the women; without an object, guérir means to get well.
In a hospital « un service » is a ward or department: « les femmes de son service » = the women on her ward.
A kind of matter; here the unknown thing in the yeast that made the women well.
A green leaf vegetable; « l'épinard » is le + épinard and « d'épinard » is de + épinard, shortened before the vowel: « les feuilles d'épinard » = spinach leaves.
Present of conseiller: « on conseille 400 microgrammes » = the advice is 400 micrograms; « on » avoids saying who gives it.
The months when a woman is pregnant (enceinte); « avant la grossesse » = before pregnancy.
Ordinal number: douze loses its -e and takes -ième; « la douzième semaine » = the twelfth week.
Plural of « une malformation », a part of the body that did not form in the usual way before birth.
Present of former, « ils/elles » form; with « se » it means to take shape: « celles-ci se forment » = these form.
Subjunctive of savoir, required after « avant que »: « avant qu'une femme sache » = before a woman knows; « se sache enceinte » = knows that she is pregnant.
« Enquêter sur » + noun = to investigate something, to look for its cause; from « une enquête », an investigation.
Of an illness: strong and serious; the same form for masculine and feminine.
Plural of « une patiente », a woman cared for by a doctor; the masculine is « un patient ».
Passé simple of constater with the subject after the verb, as in a remark inserted into a sentence; -t- is added between the two vowels.
From « une carence », a lack of something the body needs: « une alimentation carencée » = a diet that lacks something.
What a person or an animal regularly eats; « le même régime » = the same diet.
Passé simple of protéger, third person singular; the -e- after g keeps the soft sound before -a.
Feminine of « coûteux »; « peu coûteuse » = not costly, cheap.
Que + était, shortened before the vowel; after « ce que » the verb may come before its subject: « ce qu'était cette substance » = what this substance was.
Past participle of isoler, to separate a substance from everything around it; « elle fut isolée » is a passive, agreeing with « substance ».
Of Latin, the old language many scientific names come from; no capital letter in French: « le nom latin de la feuille » = the Latin name for leaf.
From découvrir (to discover): « sa découverte » = her finding, what she found.
The very beginning of a pregnancy; « dès avant la conception » = from before conception.
« Le tube neural » = the neural tube; the story says it closes within four weeks.
Of the nerves; used here in « le tube neural » = the neural tube.
« Telles que » = such as; « tel » agrees with the noun before it, here « malformations ».
A two-word medical name taken from Latin, the same as in English; the story gives it as an example of a neural tube defect: « le spina bifida ».
The amount of a medicine or a vitamin to take; « une dose plus élevée » = a higher dose.
Feminine of « élevé »; « plus élevée » = higher.
The year of Ashoka's war, counted before Christ: « environ 261 ans av. J.-C. » = about 261 BC.
Short for « avant »: « av. J.-C. » = avant Jésus-Christ, the French for BC.
The Indian king of this story, called emperor at B2; « le roi Ashoka » = King Ashoka.
The man who rules a kingdom; with a name French keeps the article: « le roi Ashoka ».
Present of regretter, third person singular: « il regrette beaucoup » = he is very sorry about what happened.
Present of planter, third person singular: « il plante des arbres » = he plants trees. The noun « une plante » (a plant) looks the same.
The opposite of « l'amour ». The h is aspirated, so there is no elision: « la haine », never « l'haine ».
Ne + arrête (present of arrêter), shortened before the vowel and completed by « pas »: « la haine n'arrête pas la haine ».
Le + amour, shortened before the vowel: « la haine cesse par l'amour » = hatred ceases by love.
The pronoun « la » (here: la haine) + arrête, shortened before the vowel; the pronoun stands before the verb: « l'amour l'arrête » = love stops it.
Feminine of « oriental »: « la côte orientale » = the east coast, the coast on the eastern side of the country.
The one who wins a war or a contest: « il ne s'est pas senti vainqueur » = he did not feel like a winner.
All the people who live under one ruler or in one country: « son peuple » = his people. « Les gens » means people in general.
Past participle of creuser (to dig): « il a creusé des puits » = he dug wells; « des puits creusés » = wells that were dug.
Graver = to cut words into stone or metal: « faire graver » = to have something carved; « gravé dans la pierre » = carved in stone. Not the adjective « grave » (serious).
Plural of « une loi »: the rules a ruler gives to a whole country.
Plural of « un rocher », a large rock standing in the landscape; « la roche » is rock as a material.
The pronoun « la » (here: la haine) + arrêter; it stands before the infinitive: « peut l'arrêter » = can stop it.
Forms of conquérir (to conquer): « a conquis » is the passé composé, « conquit » the passé simple of written narration.
The land on the east coast that Ashoka conquered; French uses the article: « le Kalinga ».
Words cut into stone so that they last; the same word as in English.
Past participle of emmener (to take someone away with you), agreeing with « personnes ».
The pain of knowing you have done wrong; it ends in -s even in the singular: « un profond remords ».
Forms of renoncer à (to give up): « a renoncé » is the passé composé, « renonça » the passé simple of written narration.
Le + enseignement, shortened before the vowel; from enseigner (to teach): « l'enseignement du Bouddha » = the Buddha's teaching.
Written with a capital letter and the article: « le Bouddha », « du Bouddha » = of the Buddha; « bouddhiste » is the adjective.
Plural of « un pilier », a tall column of stone.
Le + empire, shortened before the vowel: « dans tout l'empire » = across the whole empire.
De + ombrage, the shade that trees give: « des arbres d'ombrage » = shade trees, planted so that people can rest out of the sun.
Plural of « une religion »; the same word as in English: « la paix entre les religions ».

Ne + interdit (present of interdire, to forbid), shortened before the vowel: « il n'interdit pas la colère »; with « aucune » there is no « pas ».

The telling of what happened: « d'après son propre récit » = by his own account.

Zahn (tooth) + Arzt (doctor): „beim Zahnarzt“ = at the dentist's.
The -in ending marks the female form; after „ist“ a profession takes no article.
Der Spiegel; „einen kleinen Spiegel“ is the accusative.
Declined form of unter- (lower): „auf seinen unteren Zähnen“; the top ones are „die oberen“.
Case-inflected forms: „eine dünne Linie“, „ein dünnes Buch“, „einen dünnen Ton“.
Die Linie: „eine dünne gelbe Linie“ = a thin yellow line.
Der Schmutz has no plural; „kein Schmutz“ = not dirt.
Die Plaque (from French): the soft film on teeth, also called „Zahnbelag“.
Die Bürste; „keine Bürste“ = no brush. The verb is bürsten.
Literally tooth-stone: plaque that has hardened.
Das Gerät: „mit einem kleinen Gerät“. Not the verb form „gerät“ (from geraten).
Literally tooth-flesh; singular in German where English says gums.
Der Termin: „einen Termin machen“ = to make an appointment.
Zwei + -mal: „zweimal am Tag“ = twice a day; likewise einmal, dreimal.
Vorder- (front) + Zähne; „Vorderzähnen“ is the dative plural.
Das Papier; „Papiers“ is the genitive: „in der Farbe alten Papiers“.
Der Belag: a layer on a surface; „Zahnbelag“ is plaque.
Der Profi, short for Professional: „nur ein Profi“ = only a professional.
„Ein leichtes Kratzen“ uses the infinitive as a noun; „kratzte“ is the Präteritum.
Der Ton: „einen dünnen Ton“ = a thin sound; plural Töne.
Blei (lead) + Stift (pen): „wie ein Bleistift auf Papier“.
Partizip II of wehtun (to hurt): „Es hat nicht wehgetan“ = it did not hurt.
Reizen, er/sie/es form: „Zahnstein reizt das Zahnfleisch“.
Plural present of fangen (to catch). Separable: … an = anfangen, to begin; „so fangen die Probleme an“ = that is how the problems begin.
At the end of a clause, „fern“ is usually the detached half of a separable verb (fernhalten, to keep away): the meaning is on the verb's card.
Partizip II of verstehen: „hat nie verstanden“ = never understood.
Bilden, er/sie/es form; reflexive „bildet sich“ = forms by itself.
Inseparable, because über- is unstressed: „was übersehen wird“ = what is missed.
Die Kreide: „hart wie Kreide“ = as firm as chalk.
Bewegen, er/sie/es form: „den keine Bürste mehr bewegt“ = that no brush shifts any more.
Die Reinigung, from reinigen (to clean); -ung nouns are always feminine.
Die Minze: the herb, and the taste of toothpaste.
Präteritum of laufen; of a line: „lief eine dünne Linie“ = a thin line ran along.
Partizip II of begreifen: „nie begriffen“ = never grasped.
Adjective erwachsen, declined: „ein erwachsener Mann“; the noun is „der Erwachsene“.
Still + sitzen written as one word; separable in the present („er sitzt still“).
Der Rand: „am Rand seiner Zähne“ = along the edge of his teeth.
Präteritum of verlaufen; of a line or path: „verlief eine dünne Linie“.
Weg + bürsten; separable, but whole here as an infinitive after „lässt sich“.
Formal: „binnen Tagen“ = within days; takes the dative.
Die Ablagerung, from ablagern (to settle): what is left behind.
Partizip II of ausbilden (to train): „der dafür ausgebildet wurde“ = who was trained for it.
Der Zeitpunkt: „zu keinem Zeitpunkt“ = at no point.
Die Zunge: „mit der Zunge über die Zähne fuhr“ = ran his tongue over his teeth.
Partizip II of reizen used as an adjective: „gereiztes Zahnfleisch“.
Die Lüge (the lie); the same form is the du-imperative of lügen: „Lüge nicht“ = do not lie.
Adjective with the neuter ending: „ein buddhistisches Buch“; lowercase, unlike the noun Buddhist.
Dhammapada verse 246, which lists the five precepts.
Dhammapada verse 247, the verse about the root.
Du-imperative of verletzen: „Verletze kein Lebewesen“ = do not harm any living thing.
Leben + Wesen; the same form in the singular and the plural.
Du-imperative of nehmen, with the vowel change e → i: „Nimm nicht, was dir nicht gehört“.
„Sei treu“ = be faithful; from the same root as trauen (to trust).
Trüben, er/sie/es form: „was den Geist trübt“ = what clouds the mind.
Graben, er/sie/es form, with the vowel change a → ä. Separable: … aus = ausgraben, to dig up; „gräbt seine eigene Wurzel aus“ = digs up his own root.
Die Wurzel; „seine eigene Wurzel“ = his own root.
Bestrafen, er/sie/es form („niemand bestraft ihn“) and Partizip II („wird nicht bestraft“); inseparable.
Die Strafe: „Die Lüge ist die Strafe“ = the lie is the punishment.
Die Übersetzung, from übersetzen; -ung nouns are feminine.
Partizip II of aufschlagen: to open a book; „hat es aufgeschlagen“.
„Sich die Zeit vertreiben“ = to pass the time; inseparable.
Versprechen (verb), er/sie/es form; the noun „das Versprechen“ has its own card.
Un- + Wahrheit (truth): „Unwahrheit sprechen“ = to speak untruth.
Infinitive: „Unwahrheit sprechen“; the er/sie/es form is „spricht“.
Der Partner; „zum Partner eines anderen gehen“ = to go to another's partner.
Der Richter; „keinen Richter“ is the accusative.
Ausreißen, er/sie/es form, joined at the end of a relative clause: „der seine eigene Wurzel ausreißt“.
Partizip II of eingraben: „die Wurzel wieder eingegraben“ = put the root back in the ground.
Präteritum of betreffen: „Sie betraf einen Bericht“ = it concerned a report.
Ehe (marriage) + Partner; the same form in the singular and the plural.
Sünden (sins) + Liste; a compound made for the text.
„Nie verstecken muss“ = never has to hide; reflexive „sich verstecken“ = to hide oneself.
„Verstecken oder fürchten“; reflexive „sich fürchten“ = to be afraid.
Sich anfühlen, joined because the verb stands at the end of a subordinate clause: „wie sich das anfühlt“ = what that feels like.
Das Exemplar: one physical copy; „das Exemplar war Müllers Übersetzung“.
Sich verpflichten: „die ein Mensch sich verpflichtet nicht zu tun“ = that a person undertakes not to do.
Konjunktiv II of stehen: „hinter dem ein Richter stünde“ = behind which a judge would stand.
Die Belohnung, from belohnen: „weder Strafe noch Belohnung“.
Herausreißen, er/sie/es form, joined at the end of a relative clause: „der seine eigene Wurzel herausreißt“.
Stoßen, er/sie/es form, with the vowel change o → ö: „nichts stößt ihn“ = nothing pushes it.
Partizip II of halten with an adjective ending: „jedes gehaltene Versprechen“ = every promise that is kept.
Der Frieden: „der Schaden und der Frieden“.
Präteritum of graben. Separable: … ein = eingraben, to dig in, to plant back; „grub er die Wurzel wieder ein“ = he put the root back.

separable.translation: to dig in, to plant back

german.note: Die Mitternacht: „zehn nach Mitternacht“ = ten past midnight.
The German name of the Italian city Napoli.
The friend who opens the cupboard.
Die Spaghetti, plural in German as in Italian.
Die Chili: the pod („eine trockene Chili“); the spice is der Chili.
Der Herd; „vom Herd nehmen“ = to take off the heat.
„Brauner Knoblauch ist bitter“: garlic that browns turns bitter.
Nudel (noodle, pasta) + Wasser: the starchy water the pasta cooked in.
Die Schnur: „eine Chili an einer Schnur“ = a chilli on a string.
Italian: a big plate of spaghetti shared with friends; „spaghettata di mezzanotte“ is the Neapolitan midnight pasta.
Italian preposition in the name „spaghettata di mezzanotte“.
Italian for Mitternacht, in „spaghettata di mezzanotte“.
Die Pasta: the Italian word, common in German kitchens next to Nudeln.
Heim (home) + kommen; at the end of a subordinate clause the two halves stay together: „wenn sie hungrig heimkommen“.
Hauch (breath) + dünn: as thin as a breath; a recipe word for slicing.
Sie-imperative „Bröseln Sie“. Separable: … hinein = hineinbröseln, to crumble in; „Bröseln Sie die Chili hinein“.
Die Kelle: „eine Kelle Nudelwasser“ = a ladle of pasta water.
Die Knolle: „eine Knolle Knoblauch“ = a head of garlic.
Die Flasche: „eine Flasche Olivenöl“ = a bottle of olive oil.
Mitternacht + s + Pasta: the joining -s- is common in compounds.
Partizip II of ernähren: „hat mehr Freundschaften ernährt“ = has fed more friendships.
„In reichlich Öl“ = in plenty of oil; undeclined before a noun.
Die Stärke: starch (from the pasta water); also means strength.
In cooking: to toss pasta in the pan so the sauce coats it.
Die Packung: „eine Packung Spaghetti“ = a packet of spaghetti.
From Mitternacht with umlaut and -lich: „der mitternächtliche Teller Pasta“.
Sie-imperative: „Salzen Sie das Wasser großzügig“ = salt the water generously.
Blech (sheet metal) + Dach (roof): „Regen auf einem Blechdach“.
A kitchen word: to cook until done; „während die Spaghetti garen“.
Hindurchscheinen, joined at the end of a dass-clause: „dass das Licht hindurchscheint“.
Die Flamme: „bei kleiner Flamme“ = over a low flame.
Haften, er/sie/es form: „eine Soße, die haftet“ = a sauce that clings.
The small country in Southeast Asia that eliminated trachoma as a public health problem in 2026; a hyphenated name is one word for the reader.
Das Trachom: an eye infection spread by flies and dirty hands, the world's leading infectious cause of blindness.
Plural of die Fliege; the same word is the verb „fliegen“ (to fly).
Schmutzig (dirty), from der Schmutz: after „so“ it takes no ending („so schmutzig“), before a noun it is declined („schmutzige Hände“).
Die Infektion, plural Infektionen; nouns ending in -ion are always feminine.
Plural of die Wimper: „die Wimpern drehen sich nach innen“ = the lashes turn inward.
Das Auge, plural die Augen: „das Auge kratzen“ = to scratch the eye.
Die Operation: a surgical operation; -ion nouns are feminine.
The day in „am 3. September 2026“; the dot after the numeral marks an ordinal (dritten).
Augen + Infektion: a compound noun takes the gender of its last part.
Plural of der Wasserhahn (Wasser + Hahn, literally water-cock): a tap.
Vernarben, er/sie/es form, from die Narbe (scar): „Mit jeder Infektion vernarbt das Lid stärker“ = with every infection the eyelid scars more.
Infinitive of blinzeln (to blink) used as a neuter noun: „Jedes Blinzeln tut weh“ = every blink hurts.
Plural of das Antibiotikum, from Greek; almost always used in the plural.
„Sauberes Wasser macht das möglich“ = clean water makes that possible; machen + adjective, undeclined.
Timor-Leste was the 33rd country; the dot after „33.“ makes it an ordinal (dreiunddreißigste).
Die Region: „das letzte seiner Region“ = the last in its region (genitive).
Dative plural of das Tuch (cloth), plural Tücher: „getragen von … geteilten Tüchern“ = carried by shared cloths.
The year Timor-Leste became independent: 20 May 2002.
German writes a decimal comma where English writes a point: „1,3 Millionen“ = 1.3 million.
Der Feind, plural Feinde: „ein alter Feind“ = an old enemy.
Das Wunder, plural Wunder: „nicht auf ein Wunder warten“ = not to wait for a miracle.
Der Einwohner, the same form in the plural: „1,3 Millionen Einwohner“ = 1.3 million inhabitants.
Partizip II of beibringen (to teach someone something): „das Gesichtswaschen, jedem Kind beigebracht“ = face washing, taught to every child; the particle bei- stands before ge-.
Der Ratschlag, plural Ratschläge: „nur ein Ratschlag“ = only advice.
Ordinal number used as a noun: „das dritte“ = the third one (tool), „das vierte“ the fourth.
Weiter + tragen, written as one word at the end of a relative clause: „die Fliegen und schmutzige Hände weitertragen“ = that flies and dirty hands spread.
Der Schmerz, plural Schmerzen: „der Schmerz hört auf“ = the pain stops.
Das Lid, short for das Augenlid; plural die Lider.
Lid + Schlag (stroke): der Lidschlag, one blink of the eye; „bei jedem Lidschlag“ = with every blink.
Kratzen with the prefix zer-, which adds damage or destruction: „das Auge zerkratzen“ = to scratch the eye raw; inseparable.
Verdunkeln, from dunkel: „die Welt verdunkelt sich“ = the world grows dark; reflexive, inseparable.
Die Furcht, a more formal word than die Angst; no plural.
Gesicht + -s- + Waschen: the infinitive used as a neuter noun; the linking -s- joins the two parts.
The first name of the mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan (1887–1920).
Srinivasa Ramanujan (1887–1920), the self-taught Indian mathematician whose notebooks are still read today.
Fünf + zehn = 15; „ist fünfzehn“ = is fifteen (years old).
Mathe (short for Mathematik) + Buch: das Mathebuch.
Fünf + tausend, written as one word: 5,000.
The city in southern India now called Chennai, where Ramanujan worked as a clerk from 1912.
The year Ramanujan wrote to Hardy: 16 January 1913.
Der Professor, plural Professoren: „Ein Professor liest den Brief“; before a name no article: „Professor Hardy“.
The English university town where Hardy taught and Ramanujan spent five years.
Süd (south) + Indien, written as one word: „in Südindien“.
Partizip II of beschließen: „hat beschlossen, … zu finden“ = decided to find; inseparable.
The year Ramanujan became a clerk in Madras.
Tag + -s + über: „tagsüber Rechnungen, nachts Mathematik“ = sums by day, mathematics by night.
The day in „am 16. Januar 1913“; the dot makes it an ordinal (sechzehnten).
Schüchtern (shy) has no ending after sein or as an add-on („schüchtern und allein“), and is declined before a noun: „der schüchterne Mann“, „ein schüchterner Mann“.
G. H. Hardy, the Cambridge mathematician who read Ramanujan's letter and answered: come.
A hyphenated compound with a place name, one word for the reader: „dem Cambridge-Professor Hardy“ (dative).
„Sie müssten wahr sein“ = they must be true; the noun is die Wahrheit.
Inseparable: „Niemand konnte sie erfinden“ = nobody could invent them; „hat man im Ausland erfunden“, „wurde im Ausland erfunden“ = was invented abroad (Partizip II).
The year Ramanujan died, aged thirty-two.
Hyphenated compound; der Mathematiker is the person, die Mathematik the subject.
Präteritum plural of enthalten (to contain): „am Ende enthielten die Notizbücher Mathematik“; inseparable.
„Die nirgends im Buch stand“ = that was nowhere in the book.
Studieren, er/sie/es form: „Brian May studiert Physik“; a field of study takes no article.
First word of the name „Royal Society“, kept in English.
Die Royal Society, London's academy of sciences, founded in 1660.
Die Mathematik; stressed on the last syllable.
The year Ramanujan, aged fifteen, borrowed the maths book.
Fünfzehn + Jahr + -ig, used as a noun that declines like an adjective: „ein Fünfzehnjähriger“ = a fifteen-year-old (boy).
Das Büro, plural Büros, from French: „in einem Büro in Madras“.
Büro + Angestellter: an adjective used as a noun, so the ending changes: „ein Büroangestellter“, „der Büroangestellte“; after „wurde“ no article.
Plural of die Rechnung (from rechnen, to calculate): „tagsüber Rechnungen“ = sums by day.
Declined form of einsam (lonely, solitary): „einsame Jahre“ = lonely years.
Partizip I of frieren (to be cold): „voller Heimweh und frierend“ = homesick and cold.
Heim (home) + Weh (pain): das Heimweh; „voller Heimweh“ = full of homesickness.
Beweisen (to prove), the verb of der Beweis: „jedes davon selbst zu beweisen“ = to prove every one himself; inseparable.
Das Stipendium, plural Stipendien: money that lets a student study.
Das Mitglied, plural Mitglieder: „Mitglied der Royal Society“ = Fellow of the Royal Society.
Die Periode, also called die Regel or die Menstruation: the days when the lining of the womb leaves the body with some blood.
Schleim (mucus) + Haut (skin): here the lining of the womb, which grows every month and leaves the body as the period.
Gebär- (from gebären, to give birth) + Mutter: the organ where a baby grows; the everyday word, not a euphemism.
Der Zyklus, plural Zyklen: the menstrual cycle, „Ein Zyklus hat 28 Tage“.
Partizip II of abstoßen: „wird abgestoßen“ = is shed.
„Um Tag 14“ = around day 14, the middle of a 28-day cycle, when the egg is released.
Die Eizelle: Ei (egg) + Zelle (cell), the woman's egg; a compound takes the gender of its last part.
The year Arunachalam Muruganantham saw his wife's rag and set out to make a cheap pad.
The year India honoured Muruganantham with one of its highest civilian awards, the Padma Shri.
The first name of Arunachalam Muruganantham, the inventor of a low-cost pad machine, born in 1962 in Tamil Nadu.
Arunachalam Muruganantham, the Indian inventor who tested his own pads; „Murugananthams Frau“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
Der Lappen, the same form in the plural: an old piece of cloth; „einen Lappen verstecken“ = to hide a rag.
Die Binde, plural Binden: short for Damenbinde, a sanitary pad; the same word also means a bandage.
Plural of die Rupie, the Indian currency: „für wenige Rupien“ = for a few rupees.
Ehren (to honour): „ehrt“ present, „ehrte“ Präteritum, „geehrt“ Partizip II: „2016 hat Indien ihn geehrt“.
„Binden waren zu teuer“ = pads were too expensive; after sein the adjective takes no ending.
Tier + Blut: „gefüllt mit Tierblut“ = filled with animal blood; a compound takes the gender of its last part (das Blut).
Frauen + Gruppen, plural of die Frauengruppe: „Er hat sie Frauengruppen gegeben“ = he gave it to women's groups (dative plural).
Plural of die Firma: „Er gab sie Frauengruppen, nicht Firmen“ = to women's groups, not companies.
Präteritum of verleihen (to award, to confer): „2016 verlieh ihm Indien eine hohe Auszeichnung“; inseparable.
Partizip II of zurückkommen: „war zurückgekommen“ = had come back; the particle zurück- stands before ge-.
Motor + Roller: der Motorroller, a motor scooter; the same form in the plural.
Partizip II of freisetzen: „wird eine Eizelle freigesetzt“ = an egg is released; the particle frei- stands before ge-.
„Ein Zyklus hat 28 Tage“ = a cycle is 28 days (achtundzwanzig).
Plural of der Krampf, with umlaut: „Krämpfe“, dative „mit Krämpfen“.
Plural of das Hormon: „In der letzten Woche sinken die Hormone“ = in the last week the hormones fall.
Die Müdigkeit, from müde (tired); -keit nouns are feminine.
Die Laune: „schlechte Laune“ = a bad mood, a short temper.
Plural of die Träne: „Tränen ohne Grund“ = tears for no reason, tears from nowhere.
Der Wunsch, plural Wünsche: „der Wunsch nach Ruhe“ = the wish to rest.
Die Gereiztheit, from gereizt (irritated); -heit nouns are feminine.
Partizip II of demütigen (to humiliate), used here to open the sentence: „Gedemütigt verließ ihn seine Frau“.
Präteritum of sich weigern (to refuse), always reflexive and followed by zu + infinitive: „Er weigerte sich, sie zu verkaufen“.
Die Auszeichnung, from auszeichnen (to honour, to distinguish); -ung nouns are feminine.
A regular verb: spielt (present), spielte (Präteritum), gespielt (Partizip II).
The German name of Plato, the Greek philosopher (c. 428–348 BC) who wrote The Republic.
Der Akkord: several notes played together.
Der Bruch: a fraction in maths; also a break.
Der Staat: the state, and the German title of Plato's Republic, „Der Staat (Politeia)“.
Around 375 BC, when The Republic was written.
Die Harmonie: notes that sound well together.
Klatschen, er/sie/es form: „ein Kind, das im Takt klatscht“ = a child who claps in time.
Die Erziehung, from erziehen; -ung nouns are feminine.
The capital of England, where Brian May studied physics at Imperial College.
Die Band, an English loanword pronounced the English way: „Die Band heißt Queen“; plural die Bands.
The year Brian May began his doctorate at Imperial College, London.
The year Brian May finished his doctorate, thirty-seven years after starting it.
The first name of Brian May, guitarist of Queen and astrophysicist, born in London in 1947.
Die Physik: „studiert Physik“ = studies physics; no article, no plural.
Doktor + Arbeit: die Doktorarbeit, the thesis written for a doctorate.
Der Staub: „Staub im All“ = dust in space, „der Staub zwischen den Planeten“; no plural.
Die Gitarre, plural Gitarren: „spielt Gitarre“ = plays guitar, with no article.
The British rock band formed in London in 1970; its guitarist Brian May finished a doctorate in astrophysics in 2007.
Gewinnen, er/sie/es form: „Die Musik gewinnt“ = the music wins.
Sieben + und + dreißig = 37, one word; the units come before the tens.
Physik + Student; after „war“ a role takes no article: „war Physikstudent“ = was a physics student.
Das Konzert, plural Konzerte: „ihr erstes Konzert gegeben“ = gave its first concert.
Das Verhältnis: a ratio in maths; also a relationship.
First word of the name „Imperial College“, kept in English.
Das College, kept in English: Imperial College London, the university where Brian May studied physics.
Declined form of musikalisch: „die musikalische Erziehung“ = musical training.
Präteritum of kehren (to sweep, to turn). Separable: … zurück = zurückkehren, to return; „2007 kehrte Brian May zurück“ = in 2007 Brian May returned.
„37 Jahre zu spät“ = thirty-seven years late (siebenunddreißig).
Partizip II of anfangen (to begin), with ge- between the particle and the stem: an-ge-fangen.
Die Bühne: „auf der Bühne“ = on stage.
From innen (inside): „innerlich ein wenig unfertig“ = a little unfinished inside.
Unfertig (unfinished) used as a noun after „etwas“, with a capital letter and the ending -es: „etwas Unfertiges“.
Unerledigt (not dealt with) used as a noun: „ein kleines Unerledigtes“ = a small unfinished thing; it declines like an adjective.
Der Zusammenhang, plural Zusammenhänge: „den Zusammenhang sehen“ = to see the link.
Superlative of mächtig (powerful), from die Macht: „die mächtigste Lehrerin“ = the most powerful teacher.
Das Innerste, the superlative of inner used as a noun: „in das Innerste der Seele“ = into the inward places of the soul.
Takt (time, bar) + Schlag (stroke): der Taktschlag, one beat of the music.
Das Holz, plural Hölzer: „aus dem Holz eines alten Kamins“ = from the wood of an old fireplace.
Genitive of der Kamin (fireplace): „eines alten Kamins“ = of an old fireplace.
The Italian city whose sauce Artusi wrote down: „die Soße aus Bologna“.
Der Sellerie: here the stalks, not the root.
Der Wein: „etwas Wein“ = a little wine.
Italian ribbon pasta, plural in Italian and in German: „die Tagliatelle“.
Second word of „Spaghetti bolognese“, the dish as it is known outside Italy; an Italian adjective (from Bologna), written in lower case.
Der Deckel: „Legen Sie den Deckel auf“ = put the lid on.
Vorbeikommen, joined at the end of its relative clause: „von jedem, der vorbeikommt“ = from whoever passes.
Plural of der Koch, with umlaut.
Das Ausland: „im Ausland“ = abroad (literally in the out-land).
Die Geduld; the adjective is geduldig.
Erlauben, er/sie/es form: „wie die Geduld es erlaubt“ = as patience allows.
Der Schuss: literally a shot; in the kitchen „ein Schuss Wein“ = a splash of wine.
Partizip I of zischen used as an adverb: „zischend verdampfen“ = to hiss away.
„Lassen Sie ihn zischend verdampfen“ = let it hiss away; from der Dampf (steam).
The year Pellegrino Artusi printed his cookbook himself.
The first name of Pellegrino Artusi (1820–1911), the retired merchant whose cookbook holds the first written recipe for the sauce of Bologna.
Pellegrino Artusi, author of the cookbook of 1891; „Artusis Buch“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
Koch + Buch: das Kochbuch, plural Kochbücher.
Ein + und + siebzig = 71; „mit einundsiebzig“ = at seventy-one.
Der Verlag, plural Verlage: a publishing house; „Jeder Verlag sagte Nein“ = every publisher said no.
Drucken (to print): „druckt“ present, „druckte“ Präteritum, „gedruckt“ Partizip II: „Er druckt es selbst“, „hat er es selbst gedruckt“.
Partizip II of drucken used as an adjective: „das erste gedruckte Rezept“ = the first printed recipe.
„Servieren Sie die Soße mit Tagliatelle“ = serve the sauce with tagliatelle; the Sie-imperative looks like the infinitive.
Der Kaufmann, plural Kaufleute: a merchant or businessman.
Only used in the plural: „zu seinen Lebzeiten“ = in his lifetime.
Plural of die Auflage: „vierzehn Auflagen“ = fourteen editions (print runs).
„Über das Köche bis heute streiten“, „seither streiten die Köche darüber“ = cooks have argued about it ever since; streiten über + accusative.
Ruhe (rest) + Stand (state): „ein Kaufmann im Ruhestand“ = a retired merchant.
Pellegrino Artusi's age in 1891: „Pellegrino Artusi, 71“, „Er war 71“ = he was seventy-one (einundsiebzig).
Declined form of schriftlich (in writing), from schreiben: „das erste schriftliche Rezept“ = the first written recipe.
Genitive of Italien with -s: „jeder Verlag Italiens“ = every publisher in Italy.
Schmerzen (to hurt), er/sie/es form: „was mit einundsiebzig schmerzt“ = which stings at seventy-one.
Zusammen + fallen, one word after „lassen“: „in sich zusammenfallen“ = to collapse, to sink down soft.
The verb umrühren (to stir) used as a noun: „ein Umrühren“ = a stir.
Declined form of hungrig: „die lange, hungrige Geduld“ = the long, hungry patience.
A year: German says it as „neunzehnhundertzweiundsiebzig“, and a bare year can start a sentence: „1972 stirbt …“.
Separable verb: in a subordinate clause it stays whole („sobald Symptome auftreten“), in a main clause it splits („Symptome treten auf“). Separable: … auf = auftreten, to occur.
Behandeln (to treat): „behandelt“ is the Partizip II („hat behandelt“) and „behandelten“ the Präteritum plural („die jeden Biss behandelten“).
Präteritum of bescheinigen (to certify); the formal word for a written confirmation, from Bescheinigung = certificate.
Der Biss (bite); plural Bisse, genitive Bisses. Do not confuse it with „biss“ as a verb form (he bit).
The country in South America; German country names usually take no article.
Partizip II of eliminieren (to eliminate); verbs in -ieren form the participle without ge-: „hat eliminiert“.
Die Eliminierung, from eliminieren; nouns in -ung are feminine.
Fordern, er/sie/es form. „Es fordert Opfer“ = it claims victims (lives).
Impfen (to vaccinate): „impft“ is the present (Chile impft seine Hunde), „geimpft“ the Partizip II (hat geimpft).
The Swiss city where the World Health Organization has its seat; German name of Geneva.
Das Glück: „auf Glück warten“ = to wait for luck; an abstract noun used without an article.
Der Helfer; the plural has the same form, so only the article or the verb shows it: „Helfer gehen“.
Impfen (to vaccinate) + Team; the plural of das Impfteam.
Die Impfung; nouns in -ung are feminine, plural Impfungen.
Die Katze; plural Katzen: „Hunde und Katzen“ = dogs and cats.
Die Lepra, the old disease also called Hansen's disease; no plural.
From Mensch (person); „menschlich“ takes endings: „der menschliche Fall“, „Chiles letzter menschlicher Fall“ = Chile's last human case.
Das Merkwürdige is an adjective used as a noun, written with a capital: the strange thing.
Das Opfer; plural has the same form: „zehntausende Opfer“.
From sofort (immediately); „die sofortige Behandlung“ = the immediate treatment.
Das Symptom; plural Symptome: „sobald Symptome auftreten“ = as soon as symptoms appear.
Die Tollwut, the disease passed on by a bite; no plural.
From der Tod (death): „tödlich enden“ = to end fatally.
The prefix un- turns sichtbar (visible) into its opposite.
Inseparable verb; for time it takes sein: „Fünfzig Jahre vergehen“ = fifty years go by.
The US capital, where the WHO has a regional office (the Pan American Health Organization).
Welt (world) + weit: across the whole world.
Zehn + tausend as a plural noun: „zehntausende Menschen“.
Das Zertifikat; the official paper from the WHO.
Present participle of ziehen used before a noun: „von Tür zu Tür ziehende Impfteams“ = teams going door to door.
Die Überwachung, from überwachen; nouns in -ung are feminine.
In „Formel 1“ the numeral is said „eins“: „Formel eins“.
German writes a decimal comma where English writes a point: „2,3 Sekunden“ (zwei Komma drei) = 2.3 seconds.
The year of the last Formula 1 race at Sepang before 2026 (zweitausendsiebzehn); German uses the bare year, without „in“: „Er gewinnt hier auch 2017.“
The day in „der 4. Oktober“; the dot after the numeral makes it an ordinal (der vierte, am vierten).
„84 Punkte“ = eighty-four points; German says the units before the tens: vierundachtzig.
90; the tens end in -zig (neun + zig): „neunzig Minuten“ = ninety minutes, an hour and a half.
Max Verstappen, the Red Bull driver who won the Formula 1 race at Sepang on 4 October 2026, as he had won there in 2017.
The first name of Kimi Antonelli, who drives for Mercedes in Formula 1.
Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes driver who finished second at Sepang on 4 October 2026; „Antonellis Vorsprung“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
George Russell, a Mercedes driver in Formula 1; he was third at Sepang when his car stopped a few laps from the end.
The first name of Lewis Hamilton, who drives for Ferrari in Formula 1.
Lewis Hamilton, the Ferrari driver who finished third at Sepang on 4 October 2026.
First word of „Red Bull“, the name of Max Verstappen's Formula 1 team, kept in English.
Second word of „Red Bull“, Max Verstappen's Formula 1 team; „Red Bulls ersten Sieg“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
The Formula 1 team of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell; one car is „der Mercedes“, and the plural has the same form: „zwei Mercedes“.
The Formula 1 team Lewis Hamilton drives for; a team name takes no article: „für Ferrari“.
The place in Malaysia with the racing track where Formula 1 raced on 4 October 2026; place names take no article: „in Sepang“.
The country where Sepang lies; most country names are neuter and take no article: „in Malaysia“, „nach Malaysia“.
The German spelling of Singapore, where the next Formula 1 race after Sepang is held.
The country that gives the race its name: the Grand Prix von Bahrain was moved to Malaysia in 2026.
Die Formel; „die Formel 1“ (said „Formel eins“) is the car-racing series, always with the feminine article.
First word of „der Grand Prix“, French for „Großer Preis“: the name of a Formula 1 race, as in „der Grand Prix von Bahrain“.
Second word of „der Grand Prix“ (a Formula 1 race); the x is silent, as in French, and the plural has the same form.
Der Oktober; months are masculine: „am 4. Oktober“ = on 4 October.
Das Feld: in a race, all the cars together; a safety car brings the field close together again.
Formel 1 + Rennen, joined by hyphens into one neuter noun: „das Formel-1-Rennen“.
Die Meisterschaft: the contest over the whole season, decided on points; nouns in -schaft are feminine.
Der Fahrer (driver) has the same form in the plural, so „die Mercedes-Fahrer“ = the Mercedes drivers; the hyphen joins the team name to the noun.
Plural of die Position: a driver's place in the race; „viele Positionen verlieren“ = to lose many places.
Der Rang: the place in a race or a table; „auf Rang drei“ = in third place, with a plain number and no article.
Das Rennen, from the verb rennen (to run, to race); the plural has the same form: „sieben Rennen“ = seven races.
Plural of die Runde, one lap of the track: „wenige Runden vor Schluss“ = a few laps from the end.
Das Safety-Car, an English loan written with a hyphen: the car that drives ahead of the racing cars and slows the race down for a while.
Der Sieg, from siegen (to win): „sein erster Sieg“ = his first win.
Stark (strong) + Regen (rain): the compound for very heavy rain, used here without an article.
Der Start: the beginning of a race; „beim Start“ = at the start.
Start + Platz: the place a car starts from; „auf Startplatz eins“ = first on the grid.
Die Strecke: here the racing track; „auf nasser Strecke“ = on a wet track.
Der Vorsprung: how far ahead someone is; „mit 2,3 Sekunden Vorsprung“ = 2.3 seconds ahead.
Partizip II of sich verspäten, used like an adverb: „begann neunzig Minuten verspätet“ = began ninety minutes late.
Wohin names a direction (where to), wo a place (where): „Sepang, wohin der Grand Prix verlegt worden war“.
Regnen (to rain) always has the subject „es“: „es regnet“ (present), „es regnete“ (Präteritum), „es hat geregnet“ (Perfekt).
Starten (to start): „startet“ is the present, „startete“ the Präteritum, „ist gestartet“ the Perfekt, with sein because it is a movement.
Überholen is not separable, so its Partizip II has no ge-: „hat überholt“; „überholte“ and „überholten“ are the Präteritum.
Partizip II of verlegen (to move something to another place or date): „nach Malaysia verlegt“ = moved to Malaysia.
Partizip II of zusammenführen; the ge- goes between the particle and the verb. Separable: … zusammen = zusammenführen, to bring together.
Präteritum of vorfahren, written as one word at the end of a subordinate clause: „während er auf Rang drei vorfuhr“. Separable: … vor = vorfahren, to move up.
The year Ole began to make wooden toys (neunzehnhundertzweiunddreißig); German uses the bare year, without „in“: „1932 war Ole …“.
The year Ole's workshop burned down for the first time (neunzehnhundertvierundzwanzig).
The year Ole's workshop burned down for the second time (neunzehnhundertzweiundvierzig).
The year of the wooden duck: „ab 1935“ = from 1935 on.
The year Ole named his company LEGO (neunzehnhundertvierunddreißig).
The year the plastic brick was patented and Ole died (neunzehnhundertachtundfünfzig).
Elf; with a full stop it is an ordinal in a date: „am 11. März“ is read „am elften März“ = on 11 March.
Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter of this story; „Oles Werkstatt“ is the genitive, with -s and no apostrophe.
The middle name of Ole Kirk Christiansen.
The family name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the carpenter who began to make wooden toys in 1932.
Ole's son, who sent off the ducks with two coats of varnish instead of three.
The village in Denmark where Ole Kirk Christiansen had his workshop; place names take no article: „in Billund“.
The country; most country names are neuter and take no article: „in Dänemark“.
The name Ole gave his company in 1934, from the Danish for „spiel gut“ (play well); it is written in capitals and takes no article.
Der Zimmermann builds the wooden parts of houses; the plural is Zimmerleute. After sein a profession takes no article: „Ole ist Zimmermann“.
Das Spielzeug: one toy or toys in general, usually without a plural: „Spielzeug aus Holz“ = toys made of wood.
Holz (wood) + Spielzeug (toys); the last part gives the gender: das Holzspielzeug.
Das Jo-Jo, plural Jo-Jos: the toy that runs up and down a string; German writes it with J and a hyphen.
Die Ente, plural Enten: „jede Ente“ = every duck.
Die Firma, plural Firmen: „seine Firma“ = his company.
Plural noun with no singular in everyday use: „arme Eltern“ = poor parents.
Der Bahnhof, plural Bahnhöfe: „zum Bahnhof“ = to the station, „am Bahnhof“ = at the station, „vom Bahnhof“ = from the station.
Der Lack (varnish) + die Schicht (layer): die Lackschicht, plural Lackschichten; „zwei Lackschichten“ = two coats of varnish.
Die Kiste, plural Kisten: a sturdy box for packing goods.
Der Ausdruck, plural Ausdrücke: „der dänische Ausdruck für …“ = the Danish expression for …
Die Lieferung, from liefern (to deliver): „eine Lieferung Enten“ = a shipment of ducks, with no „von“.
Das Motto, plural Mottos: „wurde zum Motto“ = became the motto.
Bauen (to build) + Stein (stone): der Baustein, the small brick a child builds with.
Der Kunststoff, the usual German word for plastic: „aus Kunststoff“ = made of plastic.
Der März; months are masculine: „am 11. März“ = on 11 March.
Die Kleinigkeit, from klein (small); nouns in -keit are feminine: „keine Kleinigkeit“ = no small thing.
From Dänemark; dänisch takes the ending -en after im, dem or einem: „im dänischen Dorf“ = in the Danish village.
Partizip II of ziehen (to pull) used before a noun with an adjective ending: „eine an einer Schnur gezogene Ente“ = a duck pulled on a string.
Bestellen (to order): „bestellt“ is the present (niemand bestellt) and also the Partizip II (hat bestellt), without ge- because of the prefix be-; „bestellte“ is the Präteritum.
Lackieren, from der Lack (varnish): „lackiert“ is the present and also the Partizip II (verbs in -ieren take no ge-), „lackierte“ the Präteritum.
Brennen (to burn): „brennt“ is the present, „brannte“ the Präteritum. Separable: … ab = abbrennen, to burn down; „Die Werkstatt brennt ab“ = the workshop burns down.
Partizip II of abbrennen (to burn down); it takes sein: „ist abgebrannt“ = has burned down, „war abgebrannt“ = had burned down.
Partizip II of aufbauen (to build up); with wieder it means to rebuild: „hat sie wieder aufgebaut“ = rebuilt it.
Partizip II of abschicken (to send off); ge- stands between the particle and the stem: ab-ge-schickt.
Partizip II of zurückschicken (to send back): „hat ihn zurückgeschickt“ = sent him back.
Partizip II of nennen (to name, call); the vowel changes e → a: „hat seine Firma LEGO genannt“ = named his company LEGO.
Sparen: „Geld sparen“ = to save money; „gespart“ is the Partizip II: „hatte Geld gespart“ = had saved money.
Präteritum of sich verlegen auf + accusative, to turn to a new activity: „er verlegte sich auf Holzspielzeug“ = he turned to wooden toys.
Partizip II of patentieren; verbs in -ieren form it without ge-: „wurde patentiert“ = was patented.
The year Lucy Wills came to Bombay (neunzehnhundertachtundzwanzig); A1 tells the story in the present: „Es ist 1928“.
The city in India where the story takes place, under the name it had in 1928; city names take no article: „in Bombay“.
The first name of Lucy Wills, the doctor from England in this story.
The family name of Lucy Wills; B1 and B2 call her by it alone.
Schwanger sein = to be pregnant; „schwangere Frauen“ = pregnant women. With a capital letter it is a noun: „bei Schwangeren“ = in pregnant women.
With little colour in the face: „blass und sehr müde“ = pale and very tired.
Plural of die Fabrik (factory): „in Fabriken arbeiten“ = to work in factories.
Die Hefe (yeast) + der Aufstrich (something you spread on bread): der Hefeaufstrich.
Das Vitamin, plural die Vitamine; the stress is on the last syllable.
Die Folsäure: the vitamin of this story; die Säure = acid. It takes no article after „nehmen“: „Nehmen Sie Folsäure“.
Textil- + die Fabriken: factories where cloth is made; singular die Textilfabrik.
Forms of billig (cheap): „aus einem billigen Glas“ (dative), „billiger Hefeaufstrich“ (masculine, no article).
The year Lucy Wills wrote about what she had found (neunzehnhunderteinunddreißig); a bare year can open the sentence: „1931 hat sie …“.
Das Mikrogramm, one millionth of a gram; after a number the unit stays in the singular: „400 Mikrogramm“.
Schwanger (pregnant) + -schaft: die Schwangerschaft; „vor der Schwangerschaft“ = before pregnancy.
Das Risiko, plural die Risiken; „das Risiko für …“ = the risk of …, „das Risiko senken“ = to lower the risk.
Der Wirbel (vertebra) + die Säule (column): die Wirbelsäule, the backbone.
Die Anämie: the medical word; everyday German also says „Blutarmut“.
Plural of die Textilarbeiterin: Textil- + Arbeiterin; the ending -innen marks women.
Der Verdacht; „etwas im Verdacht haben“ = to suspect something: „Wills hatte das Essen im Verdacht“.
Präteritum of füttern (to feed an animal); „mit … füttern“ = to feed on …
Adjective of Anämie: „wurden anämisch“ = became anaemic.
Krank (ill) + die Station: the part of a hospital where patients stay; „auf ihrer Krankenstation“ = on her ward.
Der Stoff: a substance or material („der unbekannte Stoff“); the same word also means cloth.
Der Wills-Faktor: the name of the unknown substance until 1941; a personal name and a noun are joined with a hyphen.
The year the substance was found in spinach and named folic acid (neunzehnhunderteinundvierzig).
Der Spinat + die Blätter (leaves); the dative plural adds -n: „in Spinatblättern“.
Ordinal of zwölf: „bis zur zwölften Woche“ = until the twelfth week.
Plural of die Fehlbildung: fehl- (wrong) + Bildung (formation), a part of the body that has not formed as it should.
Form of schwer; with an illness it means severe: „eine schwere Anämie“. Here it is dative, because nachgehen takes the dative.
Nachgehen + dative (to look into something); in the infinitive with zu, the zu stands between particle and stem: nach-zu-gehen.
Die Ernährung, from sich ernähren (to feed oneself): everything a person eats.
Präteritum of feststellen (to find, to establish); in a subordinate clause the verb stays in one piece: „wie sie feststellte“ = as she found.
From der Mangel (lack): „mangelhaft“ means that something needed is missing.
Die Kost: what a person or an animal is given to eat; more formal than Essen.
Der Spinat, a green leaf vegetable; „aus Spinat“ = from spinach.
Partizip II of isolieren; verbs in -ieren form it without ge-: „wurde isoliert“ = was isolated.
Form of lateinisch, the adjective of Latein: „nach dem lateinischen Wort für Blatt“ = after the Latin word for leaf.
Form of gängig: what is commonly said or done; „ein gängiger Rat“ = a routine piece of advice.
Die Empfängnis: the moment a pregnancy begins; „vor der Empfängnis“ = before conception.
Plural of der Neuralrohrdefekt: das Neuralrohr (neural tube) + der Defekt (defect).
First word of the Latin medical name „Spina bifida“, a neural tube defect; German uses the Latin name unchanged: die Spina bifida.
Second word of the Latin medical name „Spina bifida“; it is written with a small letter and never stands alone.
Neural- + das Rohr (tube): das Neuralrohr; „schließt sich“ = closes.
Die Dosis, plural die Dosen: the amount of a medicine or vitamin taken at one time; „eine höhere Dosis“ = a higher dose.
The year of Ashoka's war: „etwa 261 vor Christus“ = in about 261 BC (zweihunderteinundsechzig).
The king in India (B2: emperor) of this story, about 261 BC; a person's name takes no article.
Der König, plural die Könige; „Ashoka ist ein König“ = Ashoka is a king.
Der Brunnen: a hole dug in the ground for water; the plural has the same form, die Brunnen.
Die Medizin: what helps sick people and animals; here without an article: „Es gibt Medizin“ = there is medicine.
Der Hass, the opposite of die Liebe; it has no plural and often stands without an article: „Hass endet durch Liebe“.
Die Liebe, from lieben (to love): „durch Liebe“ = by love, through love.
Ost- (east) + die Küste (coast): „an der Ostküste“ = on the east coast.
100 000, written as one word and without „ein“: „hunderttausend Menschen“ = a hundred thousand people.
Der Sieger, from siegen (to win): „wie ein Sieger“ = like a winner.
Partizip II of sich fühlen (to feel): „Er hat sich nicht wie ein Sieger gefühlt“ = he did not feel like a winner.
Leidtun is separable: at the end of a dass-clause it is one word, „dass es ihm leidtut“ = that he is sorry; in a main clause it splits: „Es tut ihm leid“.
Das Volk: all the people of a land or of a king; „für sein Volk“ = for his people.
Partizip II of graben (to dig): „hat Brunnen gegraben“ = dug wells. Before a noun it takes an adjective ending: „von gegrabenen Brunnen“ = of wells that were dug.
Meißeln: to cut into stone with a chisel (der Meißel). „Gemeißelt“ is the Partizip II; before a noun it takes an ending: „in Stein gemeißelten Bericht“ = account carved in stone.
german.translation: to carve (in stone), to chisel; carved

german.note: Dürfen (modal verb), ich/er/sie/es form: „dass man nie wütend sein darf“ = that one may never be angry.
Präteritum of erobern (to conquer, to take a land by war): „Ashoka eroberte Kalinga“.
The place on the east coast that Ashoka conquered in about 261 BC; such names mostly take no article.
Die Inschrift: words cut into stone; in- + die Schrift (writing).
Partizip II of wegbringen (weg = away + bringen); the verb is separable, so -ge- stands in the middle: „wurden weggebracht“ = were taken away.
Berichten, er/sie/es form: „Dieselbe Inschrift berichtet, dass …“ = the same inscription reports that …
Die Reue: the feeling of being deeply sorry for what one has done; „Reue empfinden“ = to feel remorse.
Die Lehre, from lehren (to teach): what a teacher teaches; „die Lehre des Buddha“ = the Buddha's teaching.
The teacher whose teaching Ashoka turned to; German says „der Buddha“, and the genitive here has no ending: „die Lehre des Buddha“.
Das Imperium: a very large land under one ruler; „überall in seinem Imperium“ = across his empire.
Plural of die Säule: a tall, round post of stone; „in Felsen und Säulen“ = into rocks and pillars.
Der Schatten (shade) + die Bäume (trees): trees planted to give shade; -n is the dative plural after „von“.
Plural of die Religion: „Frieden zwischen den Religionen“ = peace between religions.
Die Zeile: one line of a text or a poem; „eine Zeile, die zu ihm passt“ = a line that fits him.
Fünf: „Vers 5“ is read „Vers fünf“, the fifth verse of the Dhammapada.
Verbieten (to forbid), er/sie/es form; ver- is not separable: „Der Vers verbietet die Wut nicht“ = the verse does not forbid anger.
Die Wut: what a person feels who is wütend (angry); it has no plural.
Der Kaiser: a ruler above kings; „der indische Kaiser Ashoka“ = the Indian emperor Ashoka.
Stands after its noun and takes the dative: „seinem eigenen Bericht zufolge“ = according to his own account.
150 000: hundert + fünfzig + tausend, written as one word.
Partizip II of deportieren (to take people away from their land by force); verbs in -ieren form it without ge-: „wurden deportiert“ = were deported.
Überliefern, er/sie/es form: to pass something on to later times; über- is not separable here: „Die Inschrift überliefert seine Reue“.
Partizip II of siegen (to win, to be the victor): „Nachdem er gesiegt hatte“ = after he had won.
Präteritum of entsagen (to renounce, to give up for good); it takes the dative: „entsagte der Eroberung“ = renounced conquest.
Die Eroberung, from erobern (to conquer) + -ung: taking a land by war.
Das Gebot, plural die Gebote: a rule of a religion; „deren erstes Gebot“ = whose first precept.
Infinitive; with „zu“ it names the content of the precept: „nicht zu töten“ = not to kill.
Plural of das Edikt: an order that a ruler makes public; „seine Edikte“ = his edicts.
Form of medizinisch, the adjective of die Medizin: „von medizinischer Versorgung“ = of medical care (dative feminine ending -er).
Die Versorgung, from versorgen (to provide for, to care for) + -ung: „medizinische Versorgung“ = medical care.
Die Eintracht: when people or groups live together in agreement, without quarrel.
Plural of die Glaubensrichtung: der Glaube (faith) + -s- + die Richtung (direction): a religion or a branch of one.
Der Zorn: strong anger, a more literary word than die Wut; „verbietet keinen Zorn“ = forbids no anger.
Nähren: to give food to; „sich von etwas nähren“ = to feed on something. „Genährter“ is the Partizip II before a noun: „mit Hass genährter Hass“ = hatred fed with hatred.

Premiare = to give a prize or an honour: l'India lo premia (present), lo ha premiato (passato prossimo).
Caro means both dear and expensive: gli assorbenti erano troppo cari = pads were too expensive.
Plural of azienda (a company, a business): alle aziende = to the companies.
Indossare = to wear (clothes, a pad): ha indossato is the passato prossimo, indossò the passato remoto of written narration.
An official honour given by a state; it is feminine, so un'alta onorificenza = a high honour.
Un motorino, a small motorbike; from motore with the diminutive -ino.
Past participle of rilasciare: viene rilasciato un ovulo = an egg is released, a passive built with venire.
Passato remoto of conferire (to award formally): gli conferì un'onorificenza = awarded him an honour.
The year Brian May began his doctorate on interplanetary dust; said millenovecentosettanta.
The year Brian May finished the doctorate he had started in 1970; said duemilasette.
The given name of Brian May (born 1947), guitarist of Queen and doctor of astrophysics.
The British rock band, formed in London in 1970; Italian keeps the English name: i Queen.
An English word used in Italian for a music group; it is feminine and never changes: la band, le band.
Il dottorato (di ricerca) = the doctorate, a PhD; finire il dottorato = to finish the doctorate.
La polvere; a feminine noun in -e: la polvere tra i pianeti = the dust between the planets.
La chitarra; suonare la chitarra = to play the guitar.
Present of vincere, third person: la musica vince = the music wins; the participle is vinto.
Trenta + sette written as one word: trentasette anni di ritardo = thirty-seven years late.
All'università = a + l'università; università is feminine and ends in a stressed -à, so it does not change in the plural.
La tesi, plural le tesi; a doctoral thesis is a tesi di dottorato.
Il camino = the fireplace; da un vecchio camino = from an old fireplace. Not cammino (a walk), with two m.
Il legame, from legare (to tie): vedere il legame = to see the link.

Di + l'Imperial: dell'Imperial College = of Imperial College, the university in London.
L'educazione musicale = musical training; adjectives in -e have one form for both genders.

The given name of Pellegrino Artusi (1820–1911); as a common noun pellegrino means pilgrim.
Pellegrino Artusi, the retired merchant from Romagna whose 1891 cookbook holds the first printed recipe for the ragù of Bologna.
Settantuno drops its final o before anni: ha settantun anni = he is seventy-one.
Plural of editore (a publisher); the feminine is editrice.
Stampare = to print: lo stampa (present), lo ha stampato (passato prossimo), stampò (passato remoto), stampata (participle agreeing with ricetta).
Su + gli = sugli, before a masculine plural noun starting with a vowel, s + consonant or z: sugli spaghetti.
Un commerciante, from commercio; in pensione = retired.
In pensione = retired; andare in pensione = to retire.
Plural of cuoco: -co becomes -chi to keep the hard c sound.
Plural of edizione; nouns in -zione are feminine, plural -zioni.
Di + Italia = d'Italia, with the elision before the vowel: tutti gli editori d'Italia = every publisher in Italy.
Discutere = to argue, to discuss: i cuochi discutono (present); discuterne = to argue about it, with ne (of it) attached to the infinitive.
Participle of sparire; with essere it agrees with the subject: la paura è sparita = the fear was gone.
Spegnersi (reflexive) = to go out, like a light: il mondo si spegne = the world dims.
A quieter, more formal word than paura; il timore se ne andò = the dread went away.
Done or lived alone; lavoro solitario = work done alone.
Nostalgia (di casa) = the ache of missing home; pieno di nostalgia = homesick.

Plural of crampo, a sudden painful tightening of a muscle; in the period, the womb's cramps.

Plural of ormone, the body's chemical messengers; gli ormoni scendono = the hormones fall.
Present of scendere, loro form: to go down, to drop; the opposite of salire.
The noun of stanco (tired); -ezza makes a feminine noun from an adjective, like bellezza from bello.
Senza motivo = for no reason, out of nowhere.
Imperfetto of vergognarsi (reflexive), to feel shame; se ne vergognava = she was ashamed of it. The noun is la vergogna.
Participle of umiliare used as an adjective; it agrees with la moglie, so it ends in -a.
Being easily annoyed; nouns in stressed -ità are feminine and do not change in the plural.
A deep, bright happiness; è una gioia = it is a joy.
The raised floor where musicians play; sul palco = on stage.
In- + compiuto (completed); it agrees with its noun: una cosa incompiuta, lui un po' incompiuto.
L'anno dell'ultimo caso umano di rabbia in Cile.

Il continente dove la rabbia uccide ancora molte persone.
Plurale: cane, cani; "cane" è maschile e il plurale cambia la vocale finale.

Plurale di cura; qui significa il trattamento medico.

"Non aspettare la fortuna" = non sperare soltanto nel caso.
Città della Svizzera, una delle tre città del racconto.
Invariabile: non cambia mai; è un modo colloquiale di dire gratuitamente.
Finisce in -e: vale per il maschile e il femminile.
Una malattia antica; per il Cile fu l'altra eliminazione del 2026.
Il nome di mordere; "il morso di un cane" = a dog's bite.
Finisce in -e: vale per il maschile e il femminile.
Plurale di operatore: chi fa un lavoro pratico, qui i vaccinatori.
