Parola presa dal francese; in italiano è femminile: la routine.
La capitale del Cile, una delle tre città del racconto.
Plurale di sintomo: i segni di una malattia.
Il controllo continuo di una situazione; qui, dei casi di rabbia.
Participio passato di vaccinare; con "hanno" forma il passato prossimo.
Plurale di vaccinatore: chi dà i vaccini.
Il nome di vaccinare: l'azione di dare un vaccino.
La capitale degli Stati Uniti, una delle tre città del racconto.
Italian writes decimals with a comma, read "due virgola tre": 2,3 secondi = 2.3 seconds.
The year of the last Formula 1 race at Sepang before this one; nel 2017 = in 2017.
Dates use the plain number, without "of": domenica 4 ottobre = Sunday, 4 October.
Read "ottantaquattro": 84 punti = 84 points, Antonelli's lead in the championship.
Kimi Antonelli, the Mercedes driver who finished second and leads the championship.
Feminine of bagnato; it agrees with la pista: pista bagnata = wet track.
The Italian spelling of Bahrain; il Gran Premio del Bahrein = the Bahrain Grand Prix.
The Formula 1 team Max Verstappen drives for; team names take the feminine article: la Red Bull.
The season-long competition; primo nel campionato = first in the championship.
English term kept in Italian: la safety car, the car that slows the race down and leads the drivers for some laps.
The Formula 1 team Lewis Hamilton drives for; team names take the feminine article: la Ferrari.
La Formula 1 is the car racing championship of this story; Italian uses the article: la Formula 1.
Gara, plural gare (the h keeps the hard g); a sette gare dalla fine = with seven races to go.
Plural of giro; in a race un giro is one lap of the track: a pochi giri dalla fine = a few laps from the end.
Lewis Hamilton, the Ferrari driver who finished third.
First name of the Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli.
First name of the Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton.
Countries take the article in Italian (la Malesia), but not after in: in Malesia = in Malaysia.
The Formula 1 team of Kimi Antonelli and George Russell; le due Mercedes = the two Mercedes cars.
The number 90; novanta minuti = an hour and a half.
Months are masculine and written in lower case: domenica 4 ottobre 2026.
The noun of partire; alla partenza = at the start (of the race).
Piovere has no subject: piove = it rains; ha piovuto (or è piovuto) = it rained. The noun is la pioggia.
Singular of piste; here the race track: questa pista = this track.
English term kept in Italian: la pole position is first place at the start; partire dalla pole position = to start first.
Plural of posizione; perdere molte posizioni = to lose many places in a race.
Past participle of ricompattare (ri- + compatto): to bring a group close together again; with aveva it forms the trapassato prossimo.
Imperfect subjunctive of riprendere, to catch up with again; the subjunctive is required after senza che.
Past participle of risalire (ri- + salire), with essere: è risalito al terzo posto = he climbed back to third place.
George Russell, the Mercedes driver whose car stopped a few laps from the end.
Past participle of salire, with essere: il vantaggio è salito a 84 punti = the lead has grown to 84 points.
The place in Malaysia with the race track of this story; a Sepang = at Sepang.
Where the next race is; used like a city, without an article: a Singapore = in Singapore.
Past participle of spostare, to move something to another place; era stato spostato = had been moved.
A sports team; la sua squadra = his team, here Red Bull.
From superare: lo superano = they pass him; after li the participle agrees: li ha superati = he overtook them.
From torrente; ends in -e, so it is the same for masculine and feminine: una pioggia torrenziale = very heavy rain.
How far ahead someone is: con 2,3 secondi di vantaggio = 2.3 seconds ahead.

The noun of vincere; la sua prima vittoria = his first win.
Millenovecentoventiquattro: the year of the first fire in Ole's workshop; nel 1924 = in 1924.
Millenovecentotrentadue: the year the story begins; a year takes the article, il 1932, nel 1932.
Millenovecentotrentaquattro: the year Ole names his company; nel 1934 = in 1934.
Millenovecentotrentacinque: the year of the wooden duck; dal 1935 = from 1935 on.
Millenovecentoquarantadue: the year the workshop burns for the second time.
Millenovecentocinquantotto: the year of the patent for the brick, and the year Ole dies.
Feminine: l'anatra, le anatre; una drops its -a before a vowel, so un'anatra = a duck.
A business that makes or sells things; di + la becomes dell' before a vowel: la regola dell'azienda = the company's rule.
The village in Denmark where Ole Kirk Christiansen has his workshop; a Billund = in Billund.
The room where a craftsman works, here the carpenter's; it can also mean a small shop.
Past participle of brevettare, to patent; fu brevettato = was patented (passive with the passato remoto of essere).
The family name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter of this story.
From Danimarca; ends in -e, so it is the same for masculine and feminine, with the plural danesi. Not capitalised in Italian.
Countries take the article (la Danimarca), but not after in: in Danimarca = in Denmark.
Passato remoto of dedicarsi (lui/lei): si dedicò ai giocattoli = he turned to toys and gave them his time.
A person who makes things from wood (legno); it comes from fare + legname, timber.
Giocare is to play a game or with toys; gioca is the present (lui/lei) and also the tu imperative: gioca bene = play well.
From giocare, to play: un giocattolo, plural i giocattoli; giocattoli di legno = wooden toys.
Godtfred, the son of Ole Kirk Christiansen, who worked with his father.
The middle name of Ole Kirk Christiansen.
L'undici: dates take the article, and before undici it is l': l'11 marzo = (on) 11 March.
The name Ole gives his toy company, made from the Danish words for "play well".
A number of goods made or sent together: un lotto di anatre = a batch of ducks.
Months are written in lower case: l'11 marzo = (on) 11 March.
Diminutive of mattone, brick: the ending -cino makes it small; here the little brick children build with.
A short sentence that says what a person or a company believes in.
The first name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter who begins to make wooden toys in 1932.
From ordinare, to ask someone to make or bring something for you: ha ordinato (passato prossimo), ordinava (imperfect, was ordering).
Reflexive permettersi = to allow oneself, so to have enough money for something: non potevano permettersi nient'altro.
Quello shortens to quell' before a vowel: quell'anno = that year.
Present of ricevere (lui/lei): il bambino che lo riceve = the child who gets it.
From ricostruire (ri- = again + costruire): l'ha ricostruita, with the participle agreeing with la bottega; ricostruì is the passato remoto.
Ri- + prendere: to take something again, here to go and bring the boxes back.
To spend less; aveva risparmiato dei soldi = he had saved some money. On its own, risparmiare already means to save money.
Plural of scatola, a box for packing or sending things.
A thin, strong cord: tirare con uno spago = to pull on a string.
Passato remoto of spedire (lui/lei), to send goods or post; in speech: ha spedito.
Gerund of sperare: sperando di risparmiare = hoping to save; sperare takes di before an infinitive.
Plural of strato: due strati di vernice = two coats of varnish.
The clear or coloured liquid that protects wood and makes it shine.
To cover with vernice: vernicia (present, lui/lei), ha verniciato (passato prossimo), verniciare (infinitive).
A round toy that goes up and down on a string; the word does not change in the plural: uno yo-yo, gli yo-yo.
Millenovecentoventotto: the year Lucy Wills comes to Bombay; a year takes the article, il 1928, nel 1928.
Millenovecentotrentuno: the year Lucy Wills published her result.
Millenovecentoquarantuno: the year the substance was found in spinach and named folic acid.
Quattrocento: the number of micrograms of folic acid a day in this story.
Acido folico = folic acid; before a vowel the article il becomes l': l'acido.
Everything a person usually eats; a more formal word than cibo.
The illness of this story, which leaves a person pale and exhausted; una becomes un' before a vowel: un'anemia.
Masculine plural of anemico: ill with anemia.
Only in spina bifida, a medical name taken from Latin; English uses the same two words.
A city in India, under the name it had in 1928; a Bombay = in Bombay, to Bombay.
Said of something that does not have enough of what is needed: un'alimentazione carente = a deficient diet.
Tu imperative of chiedere: chiedi al tuo medico = ask your doctor; the person asked takes a.
La colonna vertebrale = the spine, literally the column of vertebrae.
The very beginning of a pregnancy; from concepire, to conceive.
Passato remoto of constatare (lui/lei): to see that something is a fact.
A hospital room with rows of beds: in corsia = on the ward. On a road, a corsia is a lane.
A soft food that you can spread: crema di lievito = yeast spread.
Feminine past participle of denominare, a formal word for giving something its name.
What a person or an animal eats every day; also a plan of eating to lose weight.
Feminine of dodicesimo, the ordinal of dodici: la dodicesima settimana = the twelfth week.
The amount of a medicine or a vitamin to take; plural: dosi.
Plural of fabbrica; -ca becomes -che to keep the hard c sound.
Singular foglia, plural foglie; do not confuse it with foglio, a sheet of paper.
Only in acido folico = folic acid, the vitamin of this story.
Present of formare (loro); si formano = they form, they take shape.
Said of an illness: una grave anemia = a severe anaemia; one form for masculine and feminine.
The months when a woman is incinta, expecting a baby.
From guarire, to cure: ha guarito (passato prossimo), guarì (passato remoto, lui/lei).
Feminine of ignoto: la sostanza ignota = the substance nobody could name yet.
Used in the feminine only: una donna incinta, le donne incinte.
Indagare su + thing: to look carefully for the cause of something.
Feminine past participle of isolare: fu isolata dagli spinaci = it was separated out of spinach.
Feminine of latino: la parola latina = the Latin word; languages take no capital letter in Italian.
The first name of Lucy Wills, the English doctor of this story.
Plural of microgrammo, a millionth of a gram: 400 microgrammi di acido folico.
Of the nerves: il tubo neurale = the neural tube.
Feminine plural of operaio, a factory worker: operaie tessili = women textile workers.
Feminine plural of pallido: with little colour in the face.
Plural of paziente, a person in a doctor's care; the word is the same for men and women, the article shows which: le pazienti.
Introduces a result (per + ciò, "for this"); a synonym of quindi.
Plural of ratto; a ratto is bigger than a topo (mouse).
Present of ridurre (lui/lei): riduce il rischio = it lowers the risk; it makes the risk smaller, it does not take it away.
Spina bifida is the medical name, taken from Latin, of one neural tube defect; in everyday Italian a spina is a thorn.
Almost always plural in Italian: gli spinaci.
Plural of tessile: le fabbriche tessili make cloth, and le operaie tessili work in them.
A long hollow form; il tubo neurale = the neural tube.
From vertebra: la colonna vertebrale = the spine, the backbone.
A substance in food that the body needs in very small amounts.
The family name of Lucy Wills; il fattore Wills = the Wills factor, the name the substance had until 1941.
Duecentosessantuno: about 261 a.C. is the year of Ashoka's war; a year takes the article, il 261, intorno al 261.

Present of adattarsi (lui/lei): si adatta bene a lui = it fits him well; the verb is reflexive and takes a.

L' = il before a vowel; con l'amore = by love, with love.
Infinitive of arrabbiarsi with ti joined to the end: non devi arrabbiarti = you must not get angry.
The king, later called emperor, of this story, who ruled in India about 261 a.C.
The teacher whose teaching Ashoka turns to; in Italian the name takes the article: il Buddha, del Buddha.
150 000, written as one word: cento + cinquanta + mila; mila is the plural of mille.

Plural of la costa, the land along the sea: sulle coste orientali = on the east coast.
Present of creare (lui/lei): l'odio crea altro odio = hate makes more hate.
Past participle of deportare (to take people away from their land by force), feminine plural to agree with persone.
Conditional of dire (lui/lei); si direbbe = one would say, it seems.
From dispiacere: era dispiaciuto = he was sorry; a woman says sono dispiaciuta.
Plural of l'editto, an order that a king or emperor makes public.
Plural of la fede; here it means religions: la concordia tra le fedi.
The lands ruled by an emperor (un imperatore); l' = lo before a vowel.

From India; adjectives of nationality take no capital letter in Italian: il re indiano.

A place name: the land on the east coast that Ashoka conquered about 261 a.C.

Feminine plural of medico used as an adjective: le cure mediche = medical care.
Plural of la medicina, what you take when you are ill; medicina is also the science of medicine.
Reflexive infinitive of nutrire; it takes di: nutrirsi del proprio contrario = to feed on its own opposite.
Plural of orientale, from oriente (the east); the opposite is occidentale.
Past participle of piantare, masculine plural to agree with alberi: alberi piantati = trees that were planted.
Plural of il pilastro, a tall upright block of stone.
All the people of a country, seen as one group, so the verb is singular: il suo popolo = his people. Persone are single persons.
Plural of il pozzo, a deep hole in the ground that gives water.
A rule of behaviour in a religion or a teaching; il primo precetto = the first precept.
The same form in the singular and the plural: il re, i re. The feminine is la regina.
Present of registrare (lui/lei): to write something down so that it is kept.
Plural of la regola: what people must or must not do.
Plural of la religione; nouns ending in -ione are feminine.
A telling of what happened, with its facts and numbers; from rendere conto, to give an account.

The pain of having done something wrong: provare or sentire rimorso = to feel remorse.

From tradurre, to translate: nella traduzione di Max Müller = in Max Müller's translation.

Passato remoto of venire (loro). With a past participle venire makes a passive: vennero uccise = furono uccise, were killed.
Present of vietare (lui/lei); vietato = forbidden, as on signs.
The person who wins (vincere); the feminine is la vincitrice.
Infinitive; per vivere = to live on, in order to live.

Singular of ojos: "contra el ojo" = against the eye; "una infección del ojo" = an eye infection.
Usually plural, as in English; the stress falls on -bió-.
Present and indefinido of curar, plural: "los antibióticos curan la infección", "curaron la infección".
Months are not capitalised in Spanish: "el 3 de septiembre de 2026".
"No esperó un milagro" = it did not wait for a miracle; esperar needs no preposition here.
"Los grifos llegaron despacio" = the taps came slowly, i.e. running water reached the villages.
"1,3 millones de habitantes" = 1.3 million people; the singular is habitante.
Spanish writes the decimal with a comma: "1,3 millones" = 1.3 million.
"Salud pública" = public health; the adjective follows the noun and agrees with it.
"Cada infección marca más el párpado" = each infection scars the eyelid more; stress on the first syllable.
"Cada parpadeo duele" = every blink hurts; the verb is parpadear.
A cloth for wiping; "los paños compartidos" = the shared cloths that spread the infection.
Past participle of compartir used as an adjective, masculine plural to agree with paños.
Present of apagar (to switch off); with se, "el mundo se apaga" = the world goes dark, like a light going out.
Indefinido of desaparecer (des- + aparecer): "el miedo desapareció" = the fear went.
Masculine: el dolor. "El dolor termina" = the pain stops; in the plural, dolores is the plain word for period cramps.
Present of marcar: "cada infección marca más el párpado" = each infection scars the eyelid more.
The formal adjective for ojo: "una infección ocular" = an eye infection; one form for masculine and feminine.
Present of oscurecer; with se, "el mundo se oscurece" = the world goes dark. Related to oscuro, dark.
A more formal word than miedo: "el temor desapareció con las moscas" = the dread went with the flies.
The year the fifteen-year-old Ramanujan borrowed the maths book.
The first name of Srinivasa Ramanujan, the Indian mathematician (1887–1920).
Srinivasa Ramanujan, the self-taught Indian mathematician who wrote to Hardy in 1913.
"Tiene quince años" = he is fifteen years old.
Usually plural in Spanish: "las matemáticas", "un libro de matemáticas".
In mathematics a demostración is a proof: "ninguna demostración" = no proofs; in everyday use, a demonstration.
Demostrar + los (los resultados): "demostrarlos todos" = to prove them all; the noun is demostración.
The city in southern India, today called Chennai, where Ramanujan worked as a clerk.
The year Ramanujan became a clerk in Madras.
The year Ramanujan wrote to Hardy in Cambridge.
The English university town where Hardy worked and Ramanujan lived for five years.
Past participle of prestar (to lend); "pidió prestado" = he borrowed, literally asked for as a loan.
"En el sur de la India" = in southern India; the points of the compass take el.
"Cuentas de día" = sums by day: the clerk's arithmetic.
Sixteen; "el 16 de enero de 1913" is the date of Ramanujan's letter.
Months are not capitalised in Spanish and take de before the year.
"Un hombre tímido" = a shy man; the feminine is tímida.
G. H. Hardy, the Cambridge mathematician who answered Ramanujan's letter.
Present and indefinido of contestar (to answer): "contestó: ven" = he answered: come.
"Un chico de quince años" = a boy of fifteen; the feminine is chica.
Forms of inventar: inventarlas = to invent them (the pages), haberlas inventado = to have invented them, se inventaron = were invented.
The year Ramanujan died, aged thirty-two.
"Tras perder su beca" = after losing his scholarship.
The person; the subject is las matemáticas.
"Miembro de la Royal Society" = Fellow of the Royal Society; same form for men and women.
First half of the English name the Royal Society, Britain's academy of sciences, which elected Ramanujan in 1918.
Second half of the Royal Society, kept in English; Spanish says "la Royal Society".
Indefinido of arruinar: "el frío arruinó su salud" = the cold broke his health.
A little older and more literary than chico: "un muchacho de quince años".
"Nostalgia de casa" = homesickness: the longing for a place you have left.
Oficina + -ista: someone who works in an office; the same form for a woman (la oficinista).
"Años de trabajo solitario" = years of working alone; the feminine is solitaria.
The year Arunachalam Muruganantham saw his wife's rag and set out to make a cheap pad.
The first name of Arunachalam Muruganantham (born 1962), the Indian inventor of a low-cost pad machine.
Arunachalam Muruganantham, the inventor from Tamil Nadu who tested his own sanitary pads.
"Esconde un trapo" = hides a rag; a trapo is a cloth for cleaning.
The monthly bleeding, also written período: "es para su periodo" = it is for her period.
"Una compresa" is a sanitary pad (in Latin America also toalla higiénica); the plural is compresas.
The currency of India; "por unas pocas rupias" = for a few rupees.
"La capa interior del útero" = the lining of the womb; stress on the first syllable.
"La capa interior del útero" = the inner layer (lining) of the womb; capa can also mean a cape.
Plural of empresa (company, firm): "no a empresas" = not to companies.
The medical word for the inner layer of the útero that builds up each month and leaves the body as the period.
Fourteen; "el día 14" is around the middle of the cycle, when an egg is released.
Twenty-eight; "un ciclo tiene 28 días" = a cycle is 28 days (about 28 at B1: unos 28).
The egg cell: "sale un óvulo" = an egg comes out; a hen's egg is un huevo.
Indefinido of conceder: "le concedió un alto honor" = awarded him a high honour.
Short for motocicleta, and so feminine: la moto, su moto.
"El endometrio … se desprende" = the lining comes away (is shed); desprenderse is reflexive.
Present of liberar; with passive se: "se libera un óvulo" = an egg is released.
Indefinido of negarse (to refuse): "se negó a venderla" = he refused to sell it; without se, negar means to deny.
The year India gave Muruganantham the Padma Shri, one of its highest civilian honours.
Indefinido of aceptar: "nadie aceptó probarla" = nobody agreed to test it.
The noun for feeling tired (cansado): "días de cansancio" = tired days.
"Era demasiado caro" = it was too expensive; after an infinitive subject (comprar compresas) the adjective is masculine singular.
Always plural in this sense: "ganas de descansar" = a wish to rest; tener ganas de = to feel like.
"Un alto honor" = a high honour; the h is silent.
Forms of honrar: "la India lo honra" (present), "lo honró" (indefinido); the h is silent.
"Bajan las hormonas" = the hormones fall; the subject often follows the verb in Spanish.
Past participle of humillar, feminine to agree with su mujer: "su mujer, humillada, se marchó".
"Lágrimas sin motivo" = tears from nowhere; stress on the first syllable.
Indefinido of marcharse: "su mujer se marchó" = his wife left; with se it means to go away.
Present of regenerar; with se, "la capa se regenera" = the lining grows back by itself.
The year Brian May began his doctorate at Imperial College, London.
Brian May (born 1947), the guitarist of Queen and an astrophysicist.
The science: "estudiante de física" = physics student. As an adjective, físico / física means physical.
The English capital; Spanish gives it its own spelling.
"Un doctorado sobre el polvo" = a doctorate on dust; the PhD degree.
"El polvo entre los planetas" = the dust between the planets; polvo is also powder.
Tocar is to touch, but with music it means to play: "toca la guitarra" (present), "tocó una guitarra" (indefinido).
"Toca la guitarra" = he plays the guitar; the article is needed after tocar.
The British rock band formed in London in 1970, whose guitarist is Brian May.
"La música gana" = the music wins; stress on the first syllable.
Present of ganar: "la música gana" = the music wins; ganar is also to earn.
The Greek philosopher (c. 428–348 BC), author of La República.
"Alrededor del año 375 antes de Cristo": the approximate date of Plato's Republic.
"Antes de Cristo" = BC, often shortened to a. C.; "después de Cristo" = AD.
In music, el pulso is the beat you count and feel; it is also the pulse in your wrist.
Same form in singular and plural: la tesis, las tesis.
"La madera de una vieja chimenea" = the wood of an old fireplace; also a chimney.
"Platón había visto la relación" = Plato had seen the link; nouns in -ción are feminine.
"La República" is Plato's dialogue about a just city, written around 375 BC.
"El ritmo y la armonía": the two parts of music in Plato's sentence.
"Los lugares más íntimos del alma" = the inward places of the soul.
Nouns in -ción are feminine: una fracción.
"Un acorde es una proporción" = a chord is a ratio.
"Un acorde es una proporción" = a chord is a ratio; nouns in -ción are feminine.
First half of Imperial College, the London university where Brian May studied physics.
Second half of the English name Imperial College, kept in English: el Imperial College.
"La educación musical" = musical training; also good manners.
"La educación musical" = musical training; the same form for masculine and feminine.
The year Brian May went back and finished his doctorate, thirty-seven years after starting it.
Present of abrir, plural: "se abren camino" = they find their way, literally open a path for themselves.
"Es una alegría" = it is a joy; the adjective is alegre.
"Feliz en el escenario" = happy on stage; not a scenario in the English sense.
In- + acabado (finished): "algo pequeño e inacabado" = a small unfinished thing; y becomes e before i-.
"Un poco incompleto por dentro" = a little unfinished inside.
"La mejor maestra" = the best teacher: feminine because la música is feminine.
Feminine of poderoso, agreeing with maestra: "la maestra más poderosa" = the most powerful teacher.
Imperfecto of referirse: "se refería a aprender a tocar" = he meant learning to play.
The year Artusi printed his cookbook at his own expense.
The first name of Pellegrino Artusi (1820–1911), author of the Italian cookbook of 1891.
Pellegrino Artusi, the retired merchant whose 1891 cookbook holds the first printed recipe for the sauce of Bologna.
"Setenta y un años" = seventy-one years; uno shortens to un before años.
Present and indefinido of imprimir: "él mismo lo imprime" = he prints it himself.
The city in northern Italy, home of ragù and tagliatelle: "la salsa de Bolonia".
Tú command of picar, to chop: "pica una cebolla" = chop an onion.
With onion and carrot, the base of the sauce.
The wide ribbon pasta of Bologna, an Italian word used unchanged: los tagliatelle.
Tú command of servir (e → i: sirve) with la attached (la salsa); the accent keeps the stress on sír-.
"Espaguetis a la boloñesa" = spaghetti bolognese; the ñ replaces Italian gn.
"Todos los editores de Italia" = every publisher in Italy.
"Mil ejemplares" = a thousand copies of a book; the singular is ejemplar.
"Los cocineros todavía discuten" = cooks still argue; the feminine is cocinera.
Evaporarse: "deja que se evapore" (present subjunctive after dejar que), "se deja evaporar" = is left to evaporate.
Plural of edición; nouns in -ción are feminine and drop the accent in the plural.
Irregular past participle of imprimir as an adjective, feminine to agree with receta: "la primera receta impresa".
"Tan finos como permita la paciencia" = as finely as patience allows.
Un editor is a publisher (the person or house that prints books), not only an editor: "los editores dicen que no".
Present of escocer (o → ue), a burning sting, here of a refusal: "algo que … escuece".
"En el extranjero" = abroad; as an adjective, extranjero means foreign.
"Un comerciante jubilado" = a retired merchant; jubilarse = to retire.
Past participle of olvidar with estar: "los editores están olvidados" = the publishers are forgotten.
Discutir usually means to argue, not to discuss calmly: "los cocineros todavía discuten" = cooks still argue.
Spanish says years as whole numbers: "en 1972" = in 1972 (mil novecientos setenta y dos).
A literary word for "in former times"; everyday Spanish says "antes".
A document that confirms a fact; "certificar" is the verb.
Pretérito indefinido of certificar (él/ella): a finished action at one moment.
The country in South America, the first there to be validated for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies.
Pretérito indefinido of consistir; "consistir en" = to consist of.
Past participle of contagiar used as an adjective; it agrees with feminine "rabia".
"Decenas de miles" = tens of thousands; "decena" is a group of ten.
Nouns in -ción are feminine: la eliminación.
One word in Spanish; it means the same as "inmediatamente".
"Lo extraño" = the strange thing: lo + adjective names an idea.
Plural of gato; the masculine plural can include female cats too.
The Swiss city where the World Health Organization has its headquarters.
Same form for masculine and feminine.
A long-lasting bacterial disease; Chile also eliminated it as a public health problem in 2026.
Feminine noun from morder (to bite); plural mordeduras.
Same form for masculine and feminine.
Also means "anger" in everyday Spanish; the context tells you which.
Feminine noun, close to the English word.
"Ser sinónimo de" = to be another word for, to amount to.
"Confiar en la suerte" = to trust luck; feminine noun.
Plural of síntoma, which is masculine despite ending in -a: los síntomas.
Noun from vacunar; nouns in -ción are feminine.
Pretérito indefinido of vacunar (ellos/ellas): they vaccinated.
Past participle of validar, used as an adjective: "un país validado por…".
Feminine noun; "vigilar" is to watch over.
The capital of the United States.
In "Fórmula 1" the number is read "uno": Fórmula Uno.
Spanish writes decimals with a comma and reads them "dos coma tres".
Read as a whole number, "dos mil diecisiete"; the year of the last Formula 1 race at Sepang before 2026.
In dates Spanish uses the plain number, not an ordinal: "el 4 de octubre" is read "el cuatro de octubre".
Read "ochenta y cuatro": from 31 to 99 the tens and units are joined with "y".
Forms of adelantar (to overtake): adelantó (he) and adelantaron (they) are pretérito indefinido; adelantarlo = adelantar + lo, to overtake him.
A more formal word for "los dos"; the feminine is ambas.
Kimi Antonelli, a driver for the Mercedes team; he leads the 2026 championship after this race.
Past participle of aumentar; "ha aumentado" (pretérito perfecto) = has increased.
The Spanish spelling of Bahrain; its Grand Prix (Gran Premio de Baréin) took place in Malaysia in 2026.
Red Bull is the name of Max Verstappen's racing team; the English name is not translated.
From campeón (champion): the ranking over a whole season, won by the driver with the most points.
Plural of carrera, which means a race as well as a career: "quedan siete carreras" = seven races are left.
The closed track where the cars race: "el circuito de Sepang".
A racing team; Lewis Hamilton drives for it.
"La Fórmula 1" is the top class of car racing; Spanish writes the word with an accent and takes the article "la".
Lewis Hamilton, a driver for the Ferrari team; third in this race.
The first name of the driver Kimi Antonelli.
The first name of the driver Lewis Hamilton.
Pretérito indefinido of llover; weather verbs have no subject and are used only in the third person singular.
Present of llover (o becomes ue); Spanish needs no word for "it": "llueve mucho" = it rains hard.
The country where the Sepang circuit is; Spanish spells it with an s.
A racing team; Kimi Antonelli and George Russell drive for it.
Past participle of mojar (to wet) used as an adjective: "un circuito mojado" = a wet track.
The sports press word for a Formula 1 car, which has one seat (mono + plaza); masculine although it ends in -a.
The tens from 30 to 90 end in -nta: "noventa minutos" is an hour and a half.
Months are written without a capital letter in Spanish: "el 4 de octubre".
"La parrilla (de salida)" is where the cars line up before the start; in a kitchen a parrilla is a grill.
Goes before the noun and agrees with it: "el próximo domingo", "la próxima carrera".
Plural of the noun puesto, a place in a race or ranking: "perder puestos" = to lose places.
Past participle of reagrupar (re + agrupar), masculine plural to agree with "los pilotos".
Red Bull is the name of Max Verstappen's racing team; the English name is not translated.
Pretérito indefinido of remontar: to make up lost places, to come back from behind.
Used only in the phrase "de repente" = suddenly, all at once.
George Russell, a driver for the Mercedes team, like Kimi Antonelli.
The noun of salir: in a race "la salida" is the start; on a door sign it is the exit.
A racing circuit in Malaysia; Formula 1 raced there on 4 October 2026 and, before that, in 2017.
The Spanish spelling of Singapore, where the next race takes place.
Same form for masculine and feminine: "una lluvia torrencial" = very heavy rain.
"84 puntos de ventaja" = a lead of 84 points; "con 2,3 segundos de ventaja" = 2.3 seconds ahead.
Max Verstappen, a driver for the Red Bull team and the winner of this race.
The noun that goes with ganar (to win): "su primera victoria" = his first win.
Plural of vuelta; in racing a vuelta is one lap of the circuit: "a pocas vueltas del final" = a few laps from the end.
Eleven; dates use the plain number: "el 11 de marzo" = 11 March (el once de marzo).
The year Ole's workshop burned for the first time.
The year the carpenter Ole Kirk Christiansen began to make wooden toys in Billund.
The year Ole named his company LEGO.
The year the wooden duck joined Ole's toys.
The year Ole's workshop burned for the second time.
The year the plastic brick was patented and Ole died.
Ahorrar is to save money or time; "había ahorrado" = had saved (pluscuamperfecto).
Infinitive: to pull something along the ground behind you, as a child does with a toy on a string.
Masculine: el barniz; "una capa de barniz" = a coat of varnish.
Barnizar, to cover wood with varnish: "barniza" is present, "barnizó" pretérito indefinido (z stays before a, o).
The village in Denmark where Ole Kirk Christiansen had his workshop.
Plural of capa; "dos capas de barniz" = two coats of varnish.
Spanish uses no article with a profession: "es carpintero" = he is a carpenter.
The family name of Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter of this story.
A thin rope; "con una cuerda" = on (with) a string.
Danés (masculine), danesa (feminine); "en danés" = in Danish, the language. Nationalities take no capital letter in Spanish.
Pretérito indefinido of despachar: to send goods on their way.
The country in northern Europe; its adjective is danés.
A business; "su empresa" = his company. Plural: empresas.
Encargar is to order something to be made: "encargó" is pretérito indefinido, "encargaba" the imperfect for the background.
Here the railway station; estación also means season of the year.
Ole's son, who varnished every duck again that night.
Past participle of incendiarse: "se había incendiado" = had caught fire, had burned down.
Infinitive; jugar is for games and toys, while tocar is to play an instrument.
From jugar (to play); "juguetes de madera" = wooden toys.
The middle name of Ole Kirk Christiansen.
A block for building; here the plastic brick of the toy company.
The name Ole gave his company in 1934, from the Danish for "play well".
Masculine although it ends in -a: el lema.
Pretérito indefinido of mandar, which means to send and also to tell someone to do something.
Months are not capitalised in Spanish: "el 11 de marzo".
Ole Kirk Christiansen, the Danish carpenter who made wooden toys; not the Spanish cheer "olé".
The masculine plural of padre (father) means mother and father together.
A quantity of goods sent together; partida can also be a game (of chess, of cards).
Past participle of patentar; "fue patentado" = was patented, the passive with ser.
Un pato de madera = a wooden duck; plural patos.
Pretérito indefinido of reconstruir (re- + construir); the i becomes y between vowels, as in construyó.
Plural of yoyó: one word in Spanish, with the accent on the last o.
The year the English doctor Lucy Wills came to Bombay.
The year Lucy Wills published what she had found.
The year the substance was found in spinach and named folic acid.
Cuatrocientos: "400 microgramos" = 400 micrograms, the amount for each day in this story.
Past participle of aislar, feminine to agree with "sustancia": fue aislada = it was isolated, separated from the plant.
An illness of the blood that leaves a person pale and very tired; the adjective is anémico.
Feminine plural of anémico: ill with anaemia. The accent marks the stress: a-NÉ-mi-cas.
Used almost only in the medical name "espina bífida" = spina bifida.
The city in India where Lucy Wills arrived in 1928; this was the city's name at the time.
Short for "columna vertebral", the line of bones down the back; the word also means a column.
Pretérito indefinido of comprobar, to check something and find it true: "según comprobó" = as she found.
The moment a pregnancy begins: "antes de la concepción" = before becoming pregnant.
A soft food to spread on bread, as in "crema de cacahuete" (peanut butter): "crema de levadura" = yeast spread. It also means cream.
Same form for masculine and feminine; "una dieta deficiente" lacks something the body needs.
Everything a person or an animal usually eats, not only a plan to lose weight.
The amount of a medicine or vitamin taken at one time; the plural is the same: una dosis, dos dosis.
A false friend: it never means "embarrassed". Used with estar: está embarazada = she is pregnant.
The months in which a woman carries a baby; from the same family as embarazada.
Pretérito indefinido of enfermar (ellos/ellas); "enfermar de anemia" = to fall ill with anaemia.
Here in the medical name "espina bífida" = spina bifida; in everyday Spanish an espina is a thorn or a fish bone.
A dark green leaf vegetable; Spanish often uses the plural: comer espinacas.
Masculine plural of este: estos defectos = these defects.
Present of formar (ellos/ellas); with se it describes something that happens by itself: se forman = they form.
Plural of fábrica, a building where many people make things with machines; not "fabric", which is tela.
Only used in "ácido fólico" = folic acid, the vitamin of this story; the name comes from the Latin word for leaf.
Something found after looking or studying; from hallar = to find.
The green part of a plant; "hoja" is also a sheet of paper.
Infinitive after "para": para investigar = in order to investigate.
Feminine of latino: "la palabra latina" = the word in Latin.
Lucy Wills, the English doctor of this story, who came to Bombay in 1928.
Pretérito indefinido of mejorar (ellos/ellas): las mujeres mejoraron = the women got better.
Plural of microgramo, a very small unit of weight: one millionth of a gram.
"El tubo neural" = the neural tube, the early form of the baby's brain and spine.
Feminine plural of obrero, a person who works with their hands, often in a factory.
People in a doctor's care; el paciente / la paciente has one form for both genders. As an adjective, paciente means calm and willing to wait.
Pretérito indefinido of proteger; a living being takes "a": protegió a los animales.
Feminine plural of pálido: with little colour in the face.
Plural of rata; the word is always feminine, whatever the animal's sex.
Present of reducir (él/ella): "reduce el riesgo" = it lowers the risk, it makes the risk smaller.
Present subjunctive of saber, needed after "antes de que": antes de que sepa = before she knows.
Forms of sospechar; with "de" it names what you think is the cause: sospechar de la comida = to suspect the food.
A kind of matter; here the thing in the yeast that had no name yet.
A pot with a wide mouth, usually of glass, for jam, honey or a spread.
Plural of textil, about making cloth: fábricas textiles = textile factories.
A long hollow shape: "el tubo neural" = the neural tube.
A substance in food that the body needs in small amounts; close to the English word, and feminine.
The family name of Lucy Wills; the "factor de Wills" (Wills factor) carried her name until 1941.
The year of the war in this story: "el año 261 antes de Cristo" = the year 261 BC (doscientos sesenta y uno).
Cinco: "el verso 5" = verse 5; the number comes after the noun.
Alimentar with the pronoun se attached: "alimentarse de algo" = to feed on something.
spanish.translation: to feed on, to feed itself

spanish.note: Masculine: el amor; the verb is amar, and "con amor" = with love, by love.
The Indian king, also called emperor, of this story, who won a war around 261 BC and then gave up war.
Past participle of atribuir, plural to agree with "versos": atribuidos a Buda = attributed to the Buddha.
The teacher whose teaching is Buddhism; Spanish writes Buda, without an h.
Cavar, to dig: "cava" is the present, "cavó" the pretérito indefinido, "cavados" the participle (pozos cavados = wells dug).
Present of cesar, a formal word for coming to an end: "el odio cesa" = hatred ceases; everyday Spanish says termina.
Peaceful agreement between people or groups; a formal word.
The taking of a land by war; the verb is conquistar.
Pretérito indefinido of conquistar, to take a land by war.
"Dejar constancia de algo" = to put something on record.
Present of constatar: to state what one finds to be so, without judging it.
Goes with estar: "no está contento" = he is not happy; the feminine is contenta.
Plural of credo, a set of religious beliefs; more formal than religión.
Past participle of deportar, to send people away from their land by force; feminine plural to agree with "personas".
Detener + lo: the pronoun is attached to the infinitive, "puede detenerlo" = can stop it.
Plural of edicto, an order that a ruler makes public.
The ruler of an empire (imperio); the feminine is emperatriz.
Present of encajar: "encaja con él" = it fits him, it matches him.
Goes with estar: "estar enfadado" = to be angry; in Latin America enojado is more common.
The noun that goes with enfadarse (to get angry); in Latin America people say enojo.
What a teacher teaches; from enseñar, to teach.
From ganar, to win; the feminine is ganadora.
"Grabar en piedra" = to carve in stone; grabado is the participle. Grabar also means to record sound or video.
Haber with the pronoun se attached: "podría haberse escrito" = could have been written.
Hablar, ellos/ellas form; "hablar de" = to speak of, to be about.
From India; the feminine is india. Nationalities take no capital letter in Spanish.
Words cut into stone or metal; the plural, inscripciones, loses the accent.
A strong, formal word for anger; everyday Spanish says enfado or enojo.
The land on the east coast of India that Ashoka conquered around 261 BC.
Pretérito indefinido of llevar, ellos form; "llevarse a alguien" = to take someone away.
"Mataron" is the pretérito indefinido, ellos form; with no subject it says that people were killed, without naming who did it.
Plural of medicina, something you take against an illness; la medicina is also the science of medicine.
Feminine plural of muerto. In the passive it serves as the participle of matar: "fueron muertas" = were killed.
Plural of muerto used as a noun: "contó los muertos" = he counted the dead.
The opposite of amor; the verb is odiar, to hate.
Plural of pilar, a tall column of stone.
Plantar, to plant: "plantó" is the pretérito indefinido, "plantados" the participle (árboles plantados = trees planted).
Plural of pozo, a deep hole dug in the ground to reach water.
A rule that tells the followers of a teaching how to live.
Present of prohibir; the accent on the í keeps o and i in separate syllables.
A telling of what happened; from relatar, to tell.
Plural of religión; the accent disappears in the plural.
The pain of knowing that you have done wrong; "sentir remordimiento" = to feel remorse.
Pretérito indefinido of renunciar, always with a: "renunció a la guerra" = he gave up war.
Feminine of sanitario, about care for the sick: "atención sanitaria" = health care, medical care.
Past participle of tallar, to cut a shape or words into stone or wood; masculine plural to agree with "edictos".
From traducir, to translate; the plural, traducciones, loses the accent.
