Il 16 gennaio 1913 ha fatto la cosa più coraggiosa che un uomo timido può fare. Ha scritto a uno sconosciuto in Inghilterra, con pagine di risultati. Aveva paura della risposta.
Il professore, Hardy, le ha lette e ha risposto: vieni. Ramanujan è andato a Cambridge. Oggi molti leggono ancora i suoi quaderni. Non ha aspettato: ha scritto lui.

grammar.body: After la cosa più … che, careful Italian uses the subjunctive: che un uomo timido possa fare. In speech you will also hear può; the subjunctive marks the written register.
grammar.example: Il 16 gennaio 1913 ha fatto la cosa più coraggiosa che un uomo timido possa fare.
grammar.title: Subjunctive after a superlative

grammar.body: After nessuno che (nobody who) the verb goes in the subjunctive, because such a person is missing: nessuno che lo capisse = nobody who understood him.
grammar.example: Nel 1912 è diventato impiegato a Madras: conti di giorno, matematica di notte, e nessuno che lo capisse.
grammar.title: Nessuno che + subjunctive

grammar.body: Non aveva aspettato (had not waited) looks back over the whole story from its end: imperfetto of avere plus the participle.
grammar.example: Non aveva aspettato di essere trovato.
grammar.title: Trapassato prossimo for a closing look back

paragraphs: Nel 1903, nel sud dell'India, un ragazzo di quindici anni ha preso in prestito un libro con cinquemila risultati e nessuna dimostrazione. Srinivasa Ramanujan ha deciso di trovare ogni dimostrazione da solo.
Ci sono voluti anni di lavoro solitario; era felice soltanto tra i numeri. Alla fine i suoi quaderni contenevano cose che nel libro non c'erano.
Una persona deve mangiare. Nel 1912 è diventato impiegato a Madras: conti di giorno, matematica di notte, e nessuno che lo capisse.

Il 16 gennaio 1913 ha fatto la cosa più coraggiosa che un uomo timido possa fare. Ha scritto a uno sconosciuto, il professore Hardy di Cambridge, e ha aspettato con paura. Hardy ha deciso che le pagine dovevano essere vere: nessuno poteva inventarle.

La risposta era una parola sola: vieni. Ramanujan ha passato cinque anni a Cambridge, pieno di nostalgia e di freddo, ed è morto nel 1920. I suoi quaderni si leggono ancora. Non aveva aspettato di essere trovato.

grammar.body: Prese, decise, fece, scrisse, attese, concluse, fu, trascorse, morì: the written past for events that are finished and far away, the tense of biographies.
grammar.example: La risposta fu una parola sola: vieni.
grammar.title: Passato remoto for a life told from a distance

grammar.body: Dopo aver perso (after having lost) states what happened first, before the main verb, with no subject repeated; aver drops its final e before the participle.
grammar.example: Ma una persona deve pur mangiare: dopo aver perso la borsa di studio perché non studiava altro, nel 1912 divenne impiegato.
grammar.title: Dopo aver + past participle

grammar.body: Nessuno avrebbe potuto inventarli = nobody could have invented them: conditional of avere plus the participle potuto, then the infinitive.
grammar.example: Hardy concluse che dovevano essere veri: nessuno avrebbe potuto inventarli.
grammar.title: Avrebbe potuto: the past conditional

paragraphs: Nel 1903, nel sud dell'India, un ragazzo di quindici anni prese in prestito un libro con cinquemila risultati e nemmeno una dimostrazione. Ramanujan decise di dimostrarli tutti da solo.

Ci vollero anni, e alla fine i quaderni contenevano matematica assente dal libro; era felice soltanto tra i numeri. Ma una persona deve pur mangiare: dopo aver perso la borsa di studio perché non studiava altro, nel 1912 divenne impiegato.

Il 16 gennaio 1913 fece la cosa più coraggiosa che un uomo timido possa fare. Scrisse a uno sconosciuto, il matematico Hardy di Cambridge, allegando pagine di risultati, e attese con angoscia. Hardy concluse che dovevano essere veri: nessuno avrebbe potuto inventarli.
La risposta fu una parola sola: vieni. Ramanujan trascorse cinque anni a Cambridge, tra la nostalgia di casa e il freddo, e divenne membro della Royal Society.
Il freddo gli rovinò la salute; morì nel 1920. I suoi quaderni si leggono ancora. Non aveva aspettato di essere trovato: aveva scritto.

stories.summary: Un impiegato di Madras impara la matematica da solo da un libro preso in prestito, riempie quaderni di teoremi che nessuno ha mai visto e nel 1913 scrive a uno sconosciuto.
stories.title: Il quaderno

grammar.body: In a short A1 story, "dies", "vaccinates", "pass" are all present tense, even for 1972; the dates show when it happens.
grammar.example: In 1972 a person in Chile dies of it.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: "Every year" takes a singular noun, and the verb after it follows the singular pattern.
grammar.example: Every year nobody dies.
grammar.title: Every + singular noun

paragraphs: Rabies is a dangerous disease. A dog's bite can carry it. People are afraid. In 1972 a person in Chile dies of it. The last one.
Then Chile vaccinates its dogs. Workers go from door to door. The vaccine is free.
Fifty years pass. Every year the dogs get the vaccine. Every year nobody dies.
On 14 September 2026 the World Health Organization gives Chile a certificate. No more rabies from dogs here. Chile is the first in South America.

grammar.body: What happened is in the past simple: received, came, died, vaccinated, treated, wrote. Facts that stay true use the present: is, pass, kills.
grammar.example: The last case was in 1972.
grammar.title: Past simple for events

grammar.body: The negative past is did not + the base verb: "did not wait", "did not happen", never "did not waited".
grammar.example: Chile did not wait for luck.
grammar.title: Did not + base verb

paragraphs: On 14 September 2026 Chile received a certificate for something that did not happen. It came from the World Health Organization.
For more than fifty years nobody in Chile died of rabies from a dog. The last case was in 1972.
Rabies is a disease that dogs pass on through a bite. It kills tens of thousands of people every year, mostly in Asia and Africa.
Chile did not wait for luck. Workers vaccinated dogs and cats for free, going from door to door, and doctors treated every bite quickly.
The result was a quiet success: nothing happened for fifty years, and now somebody wrote it down. Chile is the first country in South America with this certificate.

grammar.body: "Had not happened" and "had died" describe what came before the certificate in 2026: the past perfect marks the earlier past.
grammar.example: For more than fifty years, nobody there had died of rabies from a dog.
grammar.title: Past perfect for the earlier time

grammar.body: "…invisible, because the result was nothing": because gives the reason and starts a new clause.
grammar.example: The result was invisible, because the result was nothing: no case, year after year.
grammar.title: Because for a reason

paragraphs: On 14 September 2026 the World Health Organization gave Chile a certificate for something that had not happened. For more than fifty years, nobody there had died of rabies from a dog.
Rabies is a virus that dogs pass on through bites. It is almost always fatal once symptoms start, and it still kills tens of thousands of people a year. A bite used to mean fear.
The last human case was in 1972. After it came half a century of ordinary work: vaccinators at every door, free vaccines for dogs, doctors treating every bite at once.
The result was invisible, because the result was nothing: no case, year after year.
In 2026 somebody wrote it down. Chile became the first country in South America validated for eliminating dog-transmitted rabies, and its second elimination of the year, after leprosy.

grammar.body: "Almost always fatal once symptoms begin, it still kills…": an adjective phrase opens the sentence and describes its subject, rabies.
grammar.example: Almost always fatal once symptoms begin, it still kills tens of thousands a year, mostly in Asia and Africa.
grammar.title: Participle clause at the start

grammar.body: "Rabies caught from a dog" and "vaccinators going door to door": a participle after the noun does the job of a relative clause.
grammar.example: For more than fifty years, nobody in Chile had died of rabies caught from a dog.
grammar.title: Participle after a noun

paragraphs: On 14 September 2026, from Santiago, Washington and Geneva, the World Health Organization certified something that had not happened. For more than fifty years, nobody in Chile had died of rabies caught from a dog.
Rabies is passed on through a dog's bite. Almost always fatal once symptoms begin, it still kills tens of thousands a year, mostly in Asia and Africa. For a family, a bite once meant fear.

Chile's last human case was in 1972. What followed was a routine, not a miracle: vaccinators going door to door, free vaccination for dogs and cats, constant surveillance, and treatment for every bite without delay.
The strange thing about this success is that nobody sees it. Nothing happened for decades, and the nothing was the achievement.
It was the country's second elimination of 2026, after leprosy. The work nobody notices is the work that works.

stories.summary: In September 2026 the World Health Organization certifies something that did not happen: for more than fifty years, nobody in Chile has died of rabies from a dog.
stories.title: Fifty Years Without a Bite

grammar.body: In a short A1 story, "meurt", "vaccine" and "passent" are all in the present tense, even for 1972; the dates show when it happens.
grammar.example: En 1972, une personne meurt de la rage au Chili.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: "Personne" means nobody and takes "ne" before the verb: "personne ne meurt" = nobody dies. French needs no extra "pas".
grammar.example: Chaque année, personne ne meurt.
grammar.title: Ne … personne: nobody

paragraphs: La rage est une maladie dangereuse. La morsure d'un chien peut la donner. Les gens ont peur. En 1972, une personne meurt de la rage au Chili. C'est la dernière.
Le Chili vaccine ses chiens. Des employés vont de porte en porte. Le vaccin ne coûte rien.
Cinquante ans passent. Chaque année, les chiens reçoivent le vaccin. Chaque année, personne ne meurt.
Le 14 septembre 2026, l'Organisation mondiale de la santé donne un certificat au Chili. Le Chili n'a plus de rage des chiens. Il est le premier d'Amérique du Sud.

grammar.body: The passé composé is avoir (or être) in the present plus a past participle: a reçu, a vacciné, est mort. Verbs of coming and dying, like venir and mourir, take être, and the participle agrees with the subject.
grammar.example: Pendant plus de cinquante ans, personne au Chili n'est mort de la rage à cause d'un chien.
grammar.title: Passé composé for events

grammar.body: "Était" describes how things were, not a single event. It sets the scene around the passé composé actions.
grammar.example: Le résultat était un succès tranquille : rien n'est arrivé pendant cinquante ans, et maintenant quelqu'un l'a écrit.
grammar.title: Imparfait for the background

paragraphs: Le 14 septembre 2026, le Chili a reçu un certificat pour une chose qui n'est pas arrivée. Il est venu de l'Organisation mondiale de la santé.
Pendant plus de cinquante ans, personne au Chili n'est mort de la rage à cause d'un chien. Le dernier cas a eu lieu en 1972.
La rage est une maladie que les chiens transmettent par une morsure. Elle tue des dizaines de milliers de personnes par an, surtout en Asie et en Afrique.
Le Chili n'a pas attendu la chance. Des employés ont vacciné gratuitement les chiens et les chats, de porte en porte. Les médecins ont soigné chaque morsure très vite.
Le résultat était un succès tranquille : rien n'est arrivé pendant cinquante ans, et maintenant quelqu'un l'a écrit. Le Chili est le premier pays d'Amérique du Sud avec ce certificat.

grammar.body: "N'était pas arrivé" and "n'était mort" describe what came before the certificate: the plus-que-parfait is the imparfait of avoir/être plus a participle, and it marks the earlier past.
grammar.example: Pendant plus de cinquante ans, personne là-bas n'était mort de la rage à cause d'un chien.
grammar.title: Plus-que-parfait for the earlier time

grammar.body: "Que" replaces the object of the clause and links it to the noun before it: "un virus que les chiens transmettent" = a virus that dogs pass on.
grammar.example: La rage est un virus que les chiens transmettent par leurs morsures.
grammar.title: Relative pronoun que

grammar.body: "Parce que" gives the reason and starts a new clause with its own verb. Before a vowel it becomes "parce qu'".
grammar.example: Le résultat était invisible, parce que ce résultat n'était rien : aucun cas, année après année.
grammar.title: Parce que for a reason

paragraphs: Le 14 septembre 2026, l'Organisation mondiale de la santé a remis au Chili un certificat pour quelque chose qui n'était pas arrivé. Pendant plus de cinquante ans, personne là-bas n'était mort de la rage à cause d'un chien.

La rage est un virus que les chiens transmettent par leurs morsures. Elle est presque toujours mortelle quand les symptômes commencent, et elle tue des dizaines de milliers de personnes par an. Autrefois, une morsure signifiait la peur.

Le dernier cas humain date de 1972. Ensuite est venu un demi-siècle de travail ordinaire. Il y avait des vaccinateurs à chaque porte, des vaccins gratuits pour les chiens, des médecins qui soignaient chaque morsure.
Le résultat était invisible, parce que ce résultat n'était rien : aucun cas, année après année.

En 2026, quelqu'un l'a écrit. Le Chili est devenu le premier pays d'Amérique du Sud validé pour l'élimination de la rage transmise par les chiens. C'était sa deuxième élimination de l'année, après la lèpre.

grammar.body: "Presque toujours mortelle dès que les symptômes apparaissent, elle tue encore…": an adjective phrase opens the sentence and describes its subject, la rage, which comes right after the comma.
grammar.example: Presque toujours mortelle dès que les symptômes apparaissent, elle tue encore des dizaines de milliers de personnes par an, surtout en Asie et en Afrique.
grammar.title: Participle clause at the start

grammar.body: Written accounts use the passé simple (suivit, fut) where speech would use the passé composé. You read it far more than you say it.
grammar.example: Ce qui suivit fut une routine, non un miracle.
grammar.title: Passé simple in written narration

grammar.body: French has no single word for the relative "what": use ce qui when it is the subject and ce que when it is the object. "Ce qu'il y a d'étrange … c'est que" is a typical way to stress a point.
grammar.example: Ce qu'il y a d'étrange dans ce succès, c'est que personne ne le voit.
grammar.title: Ce qui / ce que for "what"

paragraphs: Le 14 septembre 2026, depuis Santiago, Washington et Genève, l'Organisation mondiale de la santé a certifié ce qui n'avait pas eu lieu. Pendant plus de cinquante ans, personne au Chili n'était mort de la rage contractée auprès d'un chien.

La rage se transmet par la morsure d'un chien. Presque toujours mortelle dès que les symptômes apparaissent, elle tue encore des dizaines de milliers de personnes par an, surtout en Asie et en Afrique. Pour une famille, une morsure signifiait jadis la peur.

Le dernier cas humain au Chili date de 1972. Ce qui suivit fut une routine, non un miracle. Il y eut des vaccinateurs de porte en porte, la vaccination gratuite des chiens et des chats, une surveillance constante et le traitement de chaque morsure sans délai.
Ce qu'il y a d'étrange dans ce succès, c'est que personne ne le voit. Il ne s'est rien passé pendant des décennies, et ce rien était l'exploit.
Ce fut la deuxième élimination du pays en 2026, après la lèpre. Le travail que personne ne remarque est celui qui marche.

stories.summary: En septembre 2026, l'Organisation mondiale de la santé certifie quelque chose qui n'est pas arrivé : depuis plus de cinquante ans, personne au Chili ne meurt de la rage à cause d'un chien.
stories.title: Cinquante ans sans morsure

grammar.body: German tells this A1 story in the present, even for 1972; the date shows when it happens. The conjugated verb stays in second position, so after "1972" it comes before the subject.
grammar.example: 1972 stirbt in Chile ein Mensch daran.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story, verb in second place

grammar.body: "Jedes Jahr" means every year: jeder changes its ending to match the gender of the noun, and Jahr is neuter. The time phrase can start the sentence, and the verb follows it.
grammar.example: Jedes Jahr stirbt niemand.
grammar.title: Jedes + neuter noun

paragraphs: Tollwut ist eine gefährliche Krankheit. Der Biss von einem Hund kann sie bringen. Die Leute haben Angst. 1972 stirbt in Chile ein Mensch daran. Es ist der letzte Fall.
Dann impft Chile seine Hunde. Helfer gehen von Tür zu Tür. Die Impfung ist kostenlos.
Fünfzig Jahre vergehen. Jedes Jahr bekommen die Hunde die Impfung. Jedes Jahr stirbt niemand.
Am 14. September 2026 gibt die Weltgesundheitsorganisation Chile ein Zertifikat. Keine Tollwut mehr von Hunden. Chile ist das erste Land in Südamerika.

grammar.body: Spoken German tells the past with the Perfekt: a helper verb in second place and the participle at the end. Verbs of movement and change, like gehen and sterben, take sein; most others take haben.
grammar.example: Helfer sind von Tür zu Tür gegangen und haben Hunde und Katzen kostenlos geimpft.
grammar.title: Perfekt: haben or sein + Partizip II at the end

grammar.body: For "to be" and "to have" German keeps the short past forms war and hatte even when everything else is in the Perfekt.
grammar.example: Der letzte Fall war 1972.
grammar.title: War and hatte for the background

grammar.body: In the Perfekt, nicht usually stands before the participle at the end: "nicht gewartet".
grammar.example: Chile hat nicht auf Glück gewartet.
grammar.title: Nicht before the final part of the sentence

paragraphs: Am 14. September 2026 hat die Weltgesundheitsorganisation Chile ein Zertifikat gegeben. Es war ein Zertifikat für etwas, das nicht passiert ist.
Mehr als fünfzig Jahre lang ist in Chile niemand an Tollwut von Hunden gestorben. Der letzte Fall war 1972.
Hunde übertragen Tollwut durch einen Biss. Jedes Jahr sterben zehntausende Menschen daran, meistens in Asien und Afrika.
Chile hat nicht auf Glück gewartet. Helfer sind von Tür zu Tür gegangen und haben Hunde und Katzen kostenlos geimpft. Ärzte haben jeden Biss schnell behandelt.
Der Erfolg war leise: Fünfzig Jahre ist nichts passiert, und jetzt hat jemand es aufgeschrieben. Chile ist das erste Land in Südamerika mit diesem Zertifikat.

grammar.body: "War passiert" and "war gestorben" describe what came before the certificate: war/hatte + Partizip II is the German past perfect. Verbs that take sein in the Perfekt also take war here.
grammar.example: Mehr als fünfzig Jahre lang war dort niemand an Tollwut von einem Hund gestorben.
grammar.title: Plusquamperfekt for the earlier time

grammar.body: A relative pronoun (das, die) sends the conjugated verb to the end of its clause. The pronoun agrees in gender with the noun it refers to, not with its role in the clause.
grammar.example: Tollwut ist ein Virus, das Hunde durch Bisse übertragen.
grammar.title: Relative clause: verb at the end

grammar.body: Weil starts a subordinate clause and sends the verb to the end: "weil das Ergebnis nichts war".
grammar.example: Das Ergebnis war unsichtbar, weil das Ergebnis nichts war: kein Fall, Jahr für Jahr.
grammar.title: Weil for a reason

paragraphs: Am 14. September 2026 gab die Weltgesundheitsorganisation Chile ein Zertifikat für etwas, das nicht passiert war. Mehr als fünfzig Jahre lang war dort niemand an Tollwut von einem Hund gestorben.

Tollwut ist ein Virus, das Hunde durch Bisse übertragen. Sie endet fast immer tödlich, sobald die Symptome beginnen, und sie tötet weltweit noch heute zehntausende Menschen im Jahr, meistens in Asien und Afrika. Ein Biss bedeutete früher Angst.
Der letzte menschliche Fall war 1972. Danach kam ein halbes Jahrhundert gewöhnlicher Arbeit: Impfteams von Tür zu Tür, kostenlose Impfungen für Hunde, Ärzte, die jeden Biss sofort behandelten.
Das Ergebnis war unsichtbar, weil das Ergebnis nichts war: kein Fall, Jahr für Jahr.
2026 schrieb es endlich jemand auf. Chile wurde das erste Land in Südamerika, das die Tollwut von Hunden eliminiert hat. Es war nach der Lepra die zweite Eliminierung des Jahres.

grammar.body: The passive is formed with werden and the participle at the end; the doer, if named, appears with durch or von. Here the bite is the means: "durch den Biss".
grammar.example: Tollwut wird durch den Biss eines Hundes übertragen.
grammar.title: Vorgangspassiv: werden + Partizip II

grammar.body: An adjective phrase can open the sentence and describe its subject; the verb then follows directly in second place and the subject comes after it.
grammar.example: Fast immer tödlich, sobald Symptome auftreten, fordert sie weltweit noch immer zehntausende Opfer im Jahr, meist in Asien und Afrika.
grammar.title: Adjective phrase in front of the verb

grammar.body: A present or past participle can stand before the noun like a compressed relative clause: "von Tür zu Tür ziehende Impfteams" = teams that go door to door. It takes adjective endings.
grammar.example: Was folgte, war Routine, kein Wunder: von Tür zu Tür ziehende Impfteams, kostenlose Impfungen für Hunde und Katzen, ständige Überwachung und die sofortige Behandlung jedes Bisses.
grammar.title: Extended participle before a noun

paragraphs: Am 14. September 2026 bescheinigte die Weltgesundheitsorganisation, von Santiago, Washington und Genf aus, etwas, das nicht geschehen war. Mehr als fünfzig Jahre lang war in Chile niemand an einer von einem Hund übertragenen Tollwut gestorben.

Tollwut wird durch den Biss eines Hundes übertragen. Fast immer tödlich, sobald Symptome auftreten, fordert sie weltweit noch immer zehntausende Opfer im Jahr, meist in Asien und Afrika. Für eine Familie bedeutete ein Biss einst Angst.

Chiles letzter menschlicher Fall war 1972. Was folgte, war Routine, kein Wunder: von Tür zu Tür ziehende Impfteams, kostenlose Impfungen für Hunde und Katzen, ständige Überwachung und die sofortige Behandlung jedes Bisses.
Das Merkwürdige an diesem Erfolg ist, dass ihn niemand sieht. Jahrzehntelang geschah nichts, und dieses Nichts war die Leistung.
Es war die zweite Eliminierung des Landes im Jahr 2026, nach der Lepra. Die Arbeit, die niemand bemerkt, ist die Arbeit, die wirkt.

stories.summary: Im September 2026 bescheinigt die Weltgesundheitsorganisation etwas, das nicht geschehen ist: Seit mehr als fünfzig Jahren ist in Chile niemand mehr an der Tollwut von einem Hund gestorben.
stories.title: Fünfzig Jahre ohne Biss

grammar.body: In this A1 story "muere", "vacuna" and "pasan" are all present tense, even for 1972; the date shows when it happens.
grammar.example: En 1972 una persona muere de rabia en Chile.
grammar.title: Present tense to tell a story

grammar.body: "Cada" never changes and always takes a singular noun without an article: cada año, cada día.
grammar.example: Cada año nadie muere.
grammar.title: Cada + singular noun, no article

paragraphs: La rabia es una enfermedad peligrosa. La mordedura de un perro puede traer la rabia. La gente tiene miedo. En 1972 una persona muere de rabia en Chile. Es la última.
Entonces Chile vacuna a sus perros. Los trabajadores van de puerta en puerta. La vacuna es gratis.
Pasan cincuenta años. Cada año los perros reciben la vacuna. Cada año nadie muere.
Es el 14 de septiembre de 2026. La Organización Mundial de la Salud da un certificado a Chile. Ya no hay rabia de perros. Es el primer país de Sudamérica.

grammar.body: Completed past events use the pretérito indefinido: recibió, murió, vacunaron, trataron. Facts that are still true stay in the present: es, mata.
grammar.example: Los trabajadores vacunaron gratis a perros y gatos, de puerta en puerta.
grammar.title: Pretérito indefinido for finished events

grammar.body: "Fue" is the pretérito indefinido of "ser" and is used for a finished fact with a date or a limit.
grammar.example: El último caso fue en 1972.
grammar.title: Ser in the past: fue

paragraphs: El 14 de septiembre de 2026 Chile recibió un certificado por algo que no pasó. Lo dio la Organización Mundial de la Salud.
Durante más de cincuenta años nadie en Chile murió de rabia por culpa de un perro. El último caso fue en 1972.
La rabia es una enfermedad que los perros transmiten con una mordedura. Cada año mata a decenas de miles de personas, sobre todo en Asia y África.
Chile no confió en la suerte. Los trabajadores vacunaron gratis a perros y gatos, de puerta en puerta. Los médicos trataron cada mordedura enseguida.
El resultado fue un éxito tranquilo: durante cincuenta años no pasó nada. Y por fin alguien lo escribió. Chile es el primer país de Sudamérica con este certificado.

grammar.body: "Había ocurrido" and "había muerto" (haber in the imperfect + participle) describe what had already happened before the certificate in 2026.
grammar.example: Durante más de cincuenta años, nadie allí había muerto de rabia por culpa de un perro.
grammar.title: Pluscuamperfecto for the earlier past

grammar.body: "Que" links a noun to a clause that describes it: un virus que los perros transmiten = a virus that dogs pass on.
grammar.example: La rabia es un virus que los perros transmiten con sus mordeduras.
grammar.title: Relative clause with "que"

grammar.body: "Solía" (imperfect of soler) + infinitive says what used to happen again and again: solía significar = used to mean.
grammar.example: Una mordedura solía significar miedo.
grammar.title: Soler + infinitive for past habit

paragraphs: El 14 de septiembre de 2026 la Organización Mundial de la Salud entregó a Chile un certificado por algo que no había ocurrido. Durante más de cincuenta años, nadie allí había muerto de rabia por culpa de un perro.

La rabia es un virus que los perros transmiten con sus mordeduras. Casi siempre es mortal cuando aparecen los síntomas. Todavía mata a decenas de miles de personas al año, sobre todo en Asia y África. Una mordedura solía significar miedo.
El último caso humano fue en 1972. Después llegó medio siglo de trabajo corriente: vacunadores en cada puerta, vacunas gratis para los perros y médicos que trataban cada mordedura de inmediato.
El resultado fue invisible, porque consistió en nada: ningún caso, año tras año.

En 2026 alguien por fin lo escribió. Chile se convirtió en el primer país de Sudamérica validado por haber eliminado la rabia transmitida por perros. Fue también su segunda eliminación del año, después de la lepra.

grammar.body: "Casi siempre mortal cuando aparecen los síntomas" opens the sentence and describes its subject, la rabia, in place of a longer "como es casi siempre mortal…".
grammar.example: Casi siempre mortal cuando aparecen los síntomas, aún mata a decenas de miles de personas al año, sobre todo en Asia y África.
grammar.title: Adjective phrase opening the sentence

grammar.body: A participle agrees with the noun it follows and works like a relative clause: "rabia contagiada por un perro" = rabies that is caught from a dog.
grammar.example: Durante más de cincuenta años, nadie en Chile había muerto de rabia contagiada por un perro.
grammar.title: Past participle after a noun

grammar.body: "Lo" before an adjective turns it into an abstract noun: lo extraño = the strange thing.
grammar.example: Lo extraño de este éxito es que nadie lo ve.
grammar.title: Lo + adjective for an abstract idea

paragraphs: El 14 de septiembre de 2026, desde Santiago, Washington y Ginebra, la Organización Mundial de la Salud certificó algo que no había ocurrido. Durante más de cincuenta años, nadie en Chile había muerto de rabia contagiada por un perro.

La rabia se transmite por la mordedura de un perro. Casi siempre mortal cuando aparecen los síntomas, aún mata a decenas de miles de personas al año, sobre todo en Asia y África. Para una familia, una mordedura era antaño sinónimo de miedo.

El último caso humano de Chile fue en 1972. Lo que siguió fue una rutina, no un milagro: vacunadores de puerta en puerta, vacunación gratuita de perros y gatos, vigilancia constante y tratamiento inmediato de cada mordedura.
Lo extraño de este éxito es que nadie lo ve. Durante décadas no pasó nada, y ese nada fue el logro.
Fue la segunda eliminación del país en 2026, después de la lepra. El trabajo que nadie nota es el trabajo que funciona.

stories.summary: En septiembre de 2026 la Organización Mundial de la Salud certifica algo que no ocurrió: durante más de cincuenta años, nadie en Chile murió de rabia por culpa de un perro.
stories.title: Cincuenta años sin una mordedura

grammar.body: In a short A1 story, "muore", "vaccina", "passano" are all present tense, even for 1972; the date shows when it happens.
grammar.example: Nel 1972 una persona in Cile muore di rabbia.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: When "nessuno" (nobody) comes before the verb, Italian does not add "non": "nessuno muore". After the verb you would need it: "non muore nessuno".
grammar.example: Ogni anno nessuno muore.
grammar.title: Nessuno takes no "non" before the verb

paragraphs: La rabbia è una malattia pericolosa. Il morso di un cane può dare la rabbia. Le persone hanno paura. Nel 1972 una persona in Cile muore di rabbia. È l'ultima.
Poi il Cile vaccina i suoi cani. Gli operatori vanno di porta in porta. Il vaccino è gratis.
Passano cinquant'anni. Ogni anno i cani ricevono il vaccino. Ogni anno nessuno muore.
Il 14 settembre 2026 l'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità dà un certificato al Cile. Qui non c'è più rabbia dai cani. Il Cile è il primo in Sud America.

grammar.body: The spoken past is a present form of avere or essere plus a past participle: "ha ricevuto", "è successo", "è morto". Verbs of change and happening, like morire and succedere, take essere, and the participle agrees with the subject.
grammar.example: Per più di cinquant'anni nessuno è morto di rabbia in Cile.
grammar.title: Passato prossimo with avere and essere

grammar.body: Italian uses "era" (imperfect) to describe how things were, while the passato prossimo tells what happened. "L'ultimo caso era del 1972" sets the date as background.
grammar.example: L'ultimo caso era del 1972.
grammar.title: Era for the background

paragraphs: Il 14 settembre 2026 il Cile ha ricevuto un certificato. Il certificato era per qualcosa che non è successo. Lo ha dato l'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità.
Per più di cinquant'anni nessuno è morto di rabbia in Cile. L'ultimo caso era del 1972.
La rabbia è una malattia che i cani trasmettono con un morso. Uccide decine di migliaia di persone ogni anno, soprattutto in Asia e in Africa.
Il Cile non ha aspettato la fortuna. Gli operatori hanno vaccinato gratis cani e gatti, di porta in porta. I medici hanno curato subito ogni morso.
Il risultato è stato un successo silenzioso. Per cinquant'anni non è successo niente e ora qualcuno lo ha scritto. Il Cile è il primo paese in Sud America con questo certificato.

grammar.body: "Era successo" and "era morto" (essere or avere in the imperfect + participle) describe what had already happened before the certificate in 2026.
grammar.example: Il 14 settembre 2026 l'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità ha dato al Cile un certificato per qualcosa che non era successo.
grammar.title: Trapassato prossimo for the earlier time

grammar.body: "Che" links a clause to a noun and is never dropped: "un virus che i cani trasmettono" = a virus that dogs pass on. It works for both people and things.
grammar.example: La rabbia è un virus che i cani trasmettono con il morso.
grammar.title: Relative "che" for the subject or object

grammar.body: "Perché" gives the reason and starts a new clause: the result was invisible because the result was nothing.
grammar.example: Il risultato era invisibile, perché il risultato era niente: nessun caso, anno dopo anno.
grammar.title: Perché for a reason

paragraphs: Il 14 settembre 2026 l'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità ha dato al Cile un certificato per qualcosa che non era successo. Per più di cinquant'anni, nessuno là era morto di rabbia per il morso di un cane.
La rabbia è un virus che i cani trasmettono con il morso. Quasi sempre è mortale quando compaiono i sintomi, e ancora oggi uccide decine di migliaia di persone all'anno. Un morso voleva dire paura.
L'ultimo caso umano è stato nel 1972. Dopo è arrivato mezzo secolo di lavoro ordinario: vaccinatori a ogni porta, vaccini gratis per i cani, medici che curavano ogni morso subito.
Il risultato era invisibile, perché il risultato era niente: nessun caso, anno dopo anno.

Nel 2026 qualcuno lo ha scritto. Il Cile è diventato il primo paese del Sud America riconosciuto per aver eliminato la rabbia trasmessa dai cani. Era la sua seconda eliminazione dell'anno, dopo la lebbra.

grammar.body: "Una volta comparsi i sintomi" means once the symptoms have appeared: a past participle that agrees with its noun replaces a whole clause. It is typical of written, formal Italian.
grammar.example: Quasi sempre mortale una volta comparsi i sintomi, uccide ancora decine di migliaia di persone all'anno, soprattutto in Asia e in Africa.
grammar.title: Absolute participle: una volta + participle

grammar.body: Written accounts of finished events often use the passato remoto (fu, seguì, accadde) where speech would use the passato prossimo. You will read it far more than you say it.
grammar.example: Per decenni non accadde nulla, e quel nulla fu l'impresa.
grammar.title: Passato remoto in written narration

grammar.body: Italian has no single word for the relative "what": it uses "quello che" (or "ciò che"). "Che cosa" is only for questions.
grammar.example: Quello che seguì fu una routine, non un miracolo: vaccinatori che andavano di porta in porta, vaccinazione gratuita per cani e gatti, sorveglianza costante e cure immediate per ogni morso.
grammar.title: "Quello che" for "what"

paragraphs: Il 14 settembre 2026, da Santiago, Washington e Ginevra, l'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità ha certificato qualcosa che non era accaduto. Per più di cinquant'anni nessuno in Cile era morto di rabbia contratta da un cane.

La rabbia si trasmette con il morso di un cane. Quasi sempre mortale una volta comparsi i sintomi, uccide ancora decine di migliaia di persone all'anno, soprattutto in Asia e in Africa. Per una famiglia, un morso significava un tempo paura.

L'ultimo caso umano in Cile fu quello del 1972. Quello che seguì fu una routine, non un miracolo: vaccinatori che andavano di porta in porta, vaccinazione gratuita per cani e gatti, sorveglianza costante e cure immediate per ogni morso.
La cosa strana di questo successo è che nessuno lo vede. Per decenni non accadde nulla, e quel nulla fu l'impresa.
Fu la seconda eliminazione dell'anno per il Paese, dopo la lebbra. Il lavoro che nessuno nota è il lavoro che funziona.

stories.summary: Nel settembre 2026 l'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità certifica qualcosa che non è successo: da più di cinquant'anni in Cile nessuno muore di rabbia per il morso di un cane.
stories.title: Cinquant'anni senza un morso

grammar.body: This A1 story is told in the present: "starts", "pass", "wins". Even 2017 is in the present here; the year shows when it happens.
grammar.example: He wins here in 2017 too.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: With he, she, it or one name the present verb takes -s: "Verstappen starts", "it rains". With a plural there is no -s: "two cars pass".
grammar.example: Two Mercedes cars pass him.
grammar.title: He/she/it + verb with -s

paragraphs: It is Sunday, 4 October 2026. Formula 1 is at Sepang in Malaysia. It rains a lot. The race starts late.
Max Verstappen starts first. Two Mercedes cars pass him. Then he passes them. He wins for Red Bull, his first win this year.
Kimi Antonelli is second. George Russell is third, but his car stops. So Lewis Hamilton is third for Ferrari.
Verstappen knows this track. He wins here in 2017 too. Next Sunday the race is in Singapore.

grammar.body: Regular verbs add -ed: started, passed, finished, stopped. Irregular verbs change: fall → fell, take → took, win → won.
grammar.example: After a safety car Verstappen passed them both and won the race.
grammar.title: Past simple: regular and irregular verbs

grammar.body: "When" joins two past actions: he was third at the moment the car stopped. Both verbs are in the past simple.
grammar.example: Russell was third when his car stopped a few laps from the end.
grammar.title: When + past simple

paragraphs: On Sunday, 4 October 2026, heavy rain fell at Sepang in Malaysia. The Formula 1 race started about ninety minutes late.
Max Verstappen started first for Red Bull, but his start was slow. The two Mercedes drivers, Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, passed him.
After a safety car Verstappen passed them both and won the race. It was his first win of 2026.
Antonelli finished second, 2.3 seconds behind. Russell was third when his car stopped a few laps from the end. Lewis Hamilton took third place for Ferrari.
Verstappen also won the last race at Sepang, in 2017. Antonelli is still first in the championship, 84 points ahead of Russell. The next race is in Singapore on Sunday.

grammar.body: "So heavy that…" links a cause to its result: the rain was very heavy, and because of it the race had to wait.
grammar.example: On Sunday, 4 October 2026, the rain over Sepang was so heavy that Formula 1 had to wait.
grammar.title: So + adjective + that

grammar.body: "Had lost" happened before "took": the past perfect (had + past participle) marks the earlier of two past events.
grammar.example: Lewis Hamilton, who had lost many places at the start, took third for Ferrari behind Antonelli.
grammar.title: Past perfect for the earlier event

grammar.body: "However" shows a contrast with the sentence before. Inside a sentence it stands between commas.
grammar.example: After a safety car, however, Verstappen overtook them both.
grammar.title: However in the middle of a sentence

paragraphs: On Sunday, 4 October 2026, the rain over Sepang was so heavy that Formula 1 had to wait. The Bahrain Grand Prix, moved to Malaysia this year, started about ninety minutes late.
Max Verstappen started first for Red Bull, but he was slow on the wet track. The two Mercedes drivers, Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, passed him immediately.
After a safety car, however, Verstappen overtook them both. He won by 2.3 seconds, his first victory of 2026 and his team's.
Russell was third when his car suddenly stopped, a few laps from the end. Lewis Hamilton, who had lost many places at the start, took third for Ferrari behind Antonelli.
Antonelli is now 84 points ahead in the championship, with seven races left. Next Sunday is Singapore. Verstappen had already won the last race at Sepang, in 2017.

grammar.body: "Had been moved" combines the past perfect (had been) with the passive (moved): the move happened before the race, and who moved it is not important.
grammar.example: On Sunday, 4 October 2026, torrential rain kept Formula 1 waiting at Sepang, where the Bahrain Grand Prix had been moved this year.
grammar.title: Past perfect passive

grammar.body: "Having lost many places" replaces "after he had lost many places": a compact, formal way to give the earlier action.
grammar.example: Antonelli finished second, while Lewis Hamilton, having lost many places at the start, recovered to third for Ferrari.
grammar.title: Perfect participle: having + past participle

grammar.body: "Once" here means "as soon as": after the safety car had done its work, the overtaking followed.
grammar.example: Once a safety car had closed the field up, Verstappen overtook them both and was never caught, finishing 2.3 seconds ahead: his first victory of 2026, and Red Bull's.
grammar.title: Once + past perfect

paragraphs: On Sunday, 4 October 2026, torrential rain kept Formula 1 waiting at Sepang, where the Bahrain Grand Prix had been moved this year. The race began about ninety minutes late, on a wet track.
Max Verstappen, first on the grid for Red Bull, got away slowly, and Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell were soon past him.
It did not last. Once a safety car had closed the field up, Verstappen overtook them both and was never caught, finishing 2.3 seconds ahead: his first victory of 2026, and Red Bull's.

Russell, running third, saw his car stop behind a safety car with a few laps remaining. Antonelli finished second, while Lewis Hamilton, having lost many places at the start, recovered to third for Ferrari.

Antonelli's championship lead over Russell has grown to 84 points with seven races remaining, the next in Singapore on Sunday. As for Verstappen, the last Formula 1 race at Sepang, in 2017, was his too.

stories.summary: On Sunday 4 October 2026 the rain kept Formula 1 waiting for an hour and a half, and then Max Verstappen won at Sepang, the track where he had last won nine years before.
stories.title: Back at Sepang, Verstappen Wins Again

grammar.body: This A1 story is told in the present: "commence", "dépasse", "gagne". Even 2017 is in the present here; the year shows when it happens.
grammar.example: Il gagne aussi ici en 2017.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: The object pronouns "le" (him) and "les" (them) stand before the verb, not after it: "le dépassent" = pass him, "il les dépasse" = he passes them.
grammar.example: Deux voitures Mercedes le dépassent.
grammar.title: Le and les before the verb

grammar.body: For the weather French uses "il" with no real meaning, like English "it": "il pleut" = it rains. "Très fort" after the verb says how much.
grammar.example: Il pleut très fort.
grammar.title: Il pleut: "il" for the weather

paragraphs: C'est le dimanche 4 octobre 2026. La Formule 1 est à Sepang, en Malaisie. Il pleut très fort. La course commence en retard.
Max Verstappen est premier au départ. Deux voitures Mercedes le dépassent. Puis il les dépasse. Il gagne pour Red Bull. C'est sa première victoire cette année.
Kimi Antonelli est deuxième. George Russell est troisième, mais sa voiture s'arrête. Alors Lewis Hamilton est troisième pour Ferrari.
Verstappen connaît ce circuit. Il gagne aussi ici en 2017. Dimanche prochain, la course est à Singapour.

grammar.body: Most verbs build the past with avoir in the present plus a past participle: a commencé, a gagné, a fini. Some participles are irregular: prendre → pris, reprendre → repris.
grammar.example: Il a gagné la course, sa première victoire de 2026.
grammar.title: Passé composé with avoir

grammar.body: Verbs of movement like tomber and partir, and all reflexive verbs (s'arrêter), take être. The participle then agrees with the subject: la pluie est tombée, la voiture s'est arrêtée.
grammar.example: Le dimanche 4 octobre 2026, une forte pluie est tombée sur Sepang, en Malaisie.
grammar.title: Passé composé with être

grammar.body: "Était" (imparfait) gives the situation, and the passé composé "s'est arrêtée" gives the event that happens in it. "Quand" joins the two.
grammar.example: Russell était troisième quand sa voiture s'est arrêtée peu avant la fin.
grammar.title: Quand: the situation and the event

paragraphs: Le dimanche 4 octobre 2026, une forte pluie est tombée sur Sepang, en Malaisie. La course de Formule 1 a commencé avec environ quatre-vingt-dix minutes de retard.
Max Verstappen est parti premier pour Red Bull, mais son départ a été lent. Les deux pilotes Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli et George Russell, l'ont dépassé.
Après une voiture de sécurité, Verstappen les a dépassés tous les deux. Il a repris la première place. Il a gagné la course, sa première victoire de 2026.
Antonelli a fini deuxième, 2,3 secondes derrière. Russell était troisième quand sa voiture s'est arrêtée peu avant la fin. Lewis Hamilton a pris la troisième place pour Ferrari.
Verstappen a aussi gagné la dernière course à Sepang, en 2017. Antonelli mène toujours le championnat, 84 points devant Russell. La prochaine course est dimanche, à Singapour.

grammar.body: "Si forte que…" links a cause to its result: the rain was very heavy, and because of it Formula 1 had to wait. The adjective agrees as usual (la pluie → forte).
grammar.example: Le dimanche 4 octobre 2026, la pluie était si forte sur Sepang que la Formule 1 a dû attendre.
grammar.title: Si + adjective + que

grammar.body: "Avait perdu" happened before "a fini": the plus-que-parfait (imparfait of avoir or être + past participle) marks the earlier of two past events.
grammar.example: Lewis Hamilton, qui avait perdu beaucoup de places au départ, a fini troisième pour Ferrari, derrière Antonelli.
grammar.title: Plus-que-parfait for the earlier event

grammar.body: "Pourtant" (however) shows a contrast with the sentence before. Inside a sentence it stands between commas.
grammar.example: Après une voiture de sécurité, pourtant, Verstappen les a doublés tous les deux.
grammar.title: Pourtant in the middle of a sentence

paragraphs: Le dimanche 4 octobre 2026, la pluie était si forte sur Sepang que la Formule 1 a dû attendre. Le Grand Prix de Bahreïn, déplacé en Malaisie cette année, a commencé avec environ quatre-vingt-dix minutes de retard.
Max Verstappen partait en pole position pour Red Bull, mais il a été lent sur la piste mouillée. Les deux pilotes Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli et George Russell, l'ont aussitôt dépassé.
Après une voiture de sécurité, pourtant, Verstappen les a doublés tous les deux. Il a gagné avec 2,3 secondes d'avance, sa première victoire de 2026 et la première de son équipe.
Russell était troisième quand sa voiture s'est soudain arrêtée, peu avant la fin. Lewis Hamilton, qui avait perdu beaucoup de places au départ, a fini troisième pour Ferrari, derrière Antonelli.
Antonelli mène maintenant le championnat avec 84 points d'avance, à sept courses de la fin. Dimanche prochain, c'est Singapour. Verstappen avait déjà gagné la dernière course à Sepang, en 2017.

grammar.body: "Avait été déplacé" combines the plus-que-parfait (avait été) with the passive (déplacé): the move happened before the race, and who moved it is not important.
grammar.example: Le dimanche 4 octobre 2026, une pluie torrentielle fit patienter la Formule 1 à Sepang, où le Grand Prix de Bahreïn avait été déplacé cette année.
grammar.title: Plus-que-parfait passive

grammar.body: "Ayant perdu de nombreuses places" replaces "après avoir perdu" or "comme il avait perdu": a compact, formal way to give the earlier action.
grammar.example: Antonelli termina deuxième, tandis que Lewis Hamilton, ayant perdu de nombreuses places au départ, remonta jusqu'à la troisième place pour Ferrari.
grammar.title: Participe composé: ayant + past participle

grammar.body: In a passé simple narrative, the action completed just before another takes the passé antérieur (passé simple of avoir or être + participle): "eut regroupé" comes first, then "doubla".
grammar.example: Dès qu'une voiture de sécurité eut regroupé le peloton, Verstappen les doubla tous les deux et ne fut plus rattrapé.
grammar.title: Dès que + passé antérieur

paragraphs: Le dimanche 4 octobre 2026, une pluie torrentielle fit patienter la Formule 1 à Sepang, où le Grand Prix de Bahreïn avait été déplacé cette année. La course débuta avec environ quatre-vingt-dix minutes de retard, sur une piste détrempée.
Max Verstappen, en pole pour Red Bull, s'élança lentement, et les deux pilotes Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli et George Russell, le doublèrent bientôt.

Cela ne dura pas. Dès qu'une voiture de sécurité eut regroupé le peloton, Verstappen les doubla tous les deux et ne fut plus rattrapé. Il termina avec 2,3 secondes d'avance : sa première victoire de 2026, et la première de Red Bull.

Russell, alors troisième, vit sa voiture s'arrêter derrière une voiture de sécurité, peu avant l'arrivée. Antonelli termina deuxième, tandis que Lewis Hamilton, ayant perdu de nombreuses places au départ, remonta jusqu'à la troisième place pour Ferrari.

Au championnat, l'avance d'Antonelli sur Russell est montée à 84 points, à sept courses de la fin, dont la prochaine dimanche à Singapour. Quant à Verstappen, la dernière course de Formule 1 à Sepang, en 2017, était déjà la sienne.

stories.summary: Le dimanche 4 octobre 2026, la pluie a fait attendre la Formule 1 pendant une heure et demie, puis Max Verstappen a gagné à Sepang, le circuit où sa dernière victoire datait de neuf ans.
stories.title: De retour à Sepang, Verstappen gagne encore

grammar.body: German tells this A1 story in the present: "startet", "überholt", "gewinnt". Even 2017 is in the present here; the year shows when it happens.
grammar.example: Er gewinnt hier auch 2017.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: The conjugated verb is always the second element of a German main clause. When "dann" opens the sentence, the subject moves behind the verb: "Dann überholt er", not "Dann er überholt".
grammar.example: Dann überholt er sie.
grammar.title: Verb in second place after dann

grammar.body: For a place in a race German uses the ordinal as a noun, with a capital letter and no article: "ist Zweiter" = is second, "wird Dritter" = comes third. For a woman it is Zweite, Dritte.
grammar.example: Kimi Antonelli ist Zweiter.
grammar.title: Erster, Zweiter, Dritter: places in a race

paragraphs: Es ist Sonntag, der 4. Oktober 2026. Die Formel 1 ist in Sepang in Malaysia. Es regnet stark. Das Rennen beginnt spät.
Max Verstappen startet als Erster. Zwei Mercedes überholen ihn. Dann überholt er sie. Er gewinnt für Red Bull, sein erster Sieg 2026.
Kimi Antonelli ist Zweiter. George Russell ist Dritter, aber sein Auto bleibt stehen. So wird Lewis Hamilton Dritter für Ferrari.
Verstappen kennt die Strecke. Er gewinnt hier auch 2017. Nächsten Sonntag ist das Rennen in Singapur.

grammar.body: Spoken German tells the past with the Perfekt: the helper verb in second place, the participle at the end. Verbs of movement or change (starten, werden, bleiben) take sein, most others take haben; "war" stays in its short past form.
grammar.example: Max Verstappen ist für Red Bull als Erster gestartet, aber sein Start war langsam.
grammar.title: Perfekt: haben or sein + Partizip II at the end

grammar.body: Verbs that begin with an unstressed prefix such as über-, ge- or be- form the Partizip II without an extra ge-: überholen → überholt, gewinnen → gewonnen, beginnen → begonnen.
grammar.example: Nach einem Safety-Car hat Verstappen beide überholt und das Rennen gewonnen.
grammar.title: Participles without ge-: überholt, gewonnen

grammar.body: "Als" means "when" for a single moment in the past. It starts a subordinate clause, so the conjugated verb ("ist") goes to the very end, after the participle.
grammar.example: Russell war Dritter, als sein Auto wenige Runden vor Schluss stehen geblieben ist.
grammar.title: Als for one moment in the past

paragraphs: Am Sonntag, dem 4. Oktober 2026, hat es in Sepang in Malaysia stark geregnet. Das Formel-1-Rennen hat etwa neunzig Minuten zu spät begonnen.
Max Verstappen ist für Red Bull als Erster gestartet, aber sein Start war langsam. Beide Mercedes-Fahrer, Kimi Antonelli und George Russell, haben ihn überholt.
Nach einem Safety-Car hat Verstappen beide überholt und das Rennen gewonnen. Es war sein erster Sieg 2026.
Antonelli ist Zweiter geworden, 2,3 Sekunden hinter Verstappen. Russell war Dritter, als sein Auto wenige Runden vor Schluss stehen geblieben ist. Lewis Hamilton ist für Ferrari Dritter geworden.
Verstappen hat 2017 auch das letzte Rennen in Sepang gewonnen. Antonelli bleibt Erster in der Meisterschaft, 84 Punkte vor Russell. Das nächste Rennen ist am Sonntag in Singapur.

grammar.body: "So stark, dass …" links a cause to its result. "Dass" starts a subordinate clause, so the conjugated verb goes to the end, after the infinitive: "warten musste".
grammar.example: Am Sonntag, dem 4. Oktober 2026, regnete es über Sepang so stark, dass die Formel 1 warten musste.
grammar.title: So … dass: a result clause

grammar.body: "Der" refers to Hamilton and sends the verb to the end of its clause. "Verloren hatte" (hatte + Partizip II) is the past perfect: he lost the places before he came third.
grammar.example: Lewis Hamilton, der beim Start viele Positionen verloren hatte, wurde für Ferrari Dritter hinter Antonelli.
grammar.title: Relative clause with the Plusquamperfekt

grammar.body: "Jedoch" (however) marks a contrast with the sentence before. In written German it often stands in the middle of the clause, after the verb and the subject, with no commas.
grammar.example: Nach einem Safety-Car überholte Verstappen jedoch beide.
grammar.title: Jedoch inside the sentence

paragraphs: Am Sonntag, dem 4. Oktober 2026, regnete es über Sepang so stark, dass die Formel 1 warten musste. Der Grand Prix von Bahrain, der dieses Jahr nach Malaysia verlegt wurde, begann etwa neunzig Minuten verspätet.
Max Verstappen startete für Red Bull als Erster, doch auf nasser Strecke war er langsam. Die beiden Mercedes-Fahrer, Kimi Antonelli und George Russell, überholten ihn sofort.
Nach einem Safety-Car überholte Verstappen jedoch beide. Er gewann mit 2,3 Sekunden Vorsprung, sein erster Sieg 2026 und der erste seines Teams.
Russell war Dritter, als sein Auto wenige Runden vor Schluss plötzlich stehen blieb. Lewis Hamilton, der beim Start viele Positionen verloren hatte, wurde für Ferrari Dritter hinter Antonelli.
Antonelli hat in der Meisterschaft nun 84 Punkte Vorsprung, bei noch sieben Rennen. Am nächsten Sonntag folgt Singapur. Schon das letzte Rennen in Sepang, 2017, hatte Verstappen gewonnen.

grammar.body: The passive of the past perfect is Partizip II + worden + war: the move happened before the race, and who moved it is not said. In the passive the participle of werden is "worden", without ge-.
grammar.example: Am Sonntag, dem 4. Oktober 2026, ließ Starkregen die Formel 1 in Sepang warten, wohin der Grand Prix von Bahrain dieses Jahr verlegt worden war.
grammar.title: Plusquamperfekt passive: verlegt worden war

grammar.body: A participle with its own complements can stand before a noun like a compressed relative clause: "dem auf Rang drei liegenden Russell" = Russell, who was lying third. The participle takes adjective endings, here the dative -en.
grammar.example: Dem auf Rang drei liegenden Russell blieb wenige Runden vor Schluss hinter einem Safety-Car das Auto stehen.
grammar.title: Extended participle before a noun

grammar.body: "Nachdem" (after) takes the tense one step further back than the main clause: Plusquamperfekt ("zusammengeführt hatte") with a main clause in the Präteritum. The main clause then starts with its verb: "überholte Verstappen".
grammar.example: Nachdem ein Safety-Car das Feld zusammengeführt hatte, überholte Verstappen beide und wurde nicht mehr eingeholt.
grammar.title: Nachdem + Plusquamperfekt

paragraphs: Am Sonntag, dem 4. Oktober 2026, ließ Starkregen die Formel 1 in Sepang warten, wohin der Grand Prix von Bahrain dieses Jahr verlegt worden war. Das Rennen begann etwa neunzig Minuten verspätet auf nasser Strecke.
Max Verstappen, für Red Bull auf Startplatz eins, kam langsam vom Fleck. Bald lagen die Mercedes-Fahrer Kimi Antonelli und George Russell vor ihm.

Dabei blieb es nicht. Nachdem ein Safety-Car das Feld zusammengeführt hatte, überholte Verstappen beide und wurde nicht mehr eingeholt. Mit 2,3 Sekunden Vorsprung holte er seinen und Red Bulls ersten Sieg 2026.

Dem auf Rang drei liegenden Russell blieb wenige Runden vor Schluss hinter einem Safety-Car das Auto stehen. Antonelli wurde Zweiter, während Lewis Hamilton nach vielen beim Start verlorenen Positionen für Ferrari auf Rang drei vorfuhr.

Antonellis Vorsprung in der Meisterschaft auf Russell ist auf 84 Punkte gewachsen, bei noch sieben Rennen, das nächste am Sonntag in Singapur. Was Verstappen betrifft: Auch das letzte Formel-1-Rennen in Sepang, 2017, ging an ihn.

stories.summary: Am Sonntag, dem 4. Oktober 2026, ließ der Regen die Formel 1 anderthalb Stunden warten, und dann gewann Max Verstappen in Sepang, auf der Strecke, auf der er zuletzt neun Jahre zuvor gewonnen hatte.
stories.title: Zurück in Sepang: Verstappen gewinnt wieder

grammar.body: This A1 story is told in the present: "empieza", "pasan", "gana". Even 2017 stays in the present here; the year shows when it happens.
grammar.example: También gana aquí en 2017.
grammar.title: Present tense, even for 2017

grammar.body: The object pronouns "lo" (him) and "los" (them) stand before the conjugated verb: "lo pasan" = they pass him, "los pasa" = he passes them.
grammar.example: Dos coches de Mercedes lo pasan.
grammar.title: Lo and los before the verb

paragraphs: Es domingo, 4 de octubre de 2026. La Fórmula 1 está en Sepang, en Malasia. Llueve mucho. La carrera empieza tarde.
Max Verstappen es el primero en la salida. Dos coches de Mercedes lo pasan. Después él los pasa. Gana con Red Bull. Es su primera victoria este año.
Kimi Antonelli es segundo. George Russell es tercero, pero su coche se detiene. Entonces Lewis Hamilton es tercero con Ferrari.
Verstappen conoce este circuito. También gana aquí en 2017. El próximo domingo la carrera es en Singapur.

grammar.body: Finished past actions take the pretérito indefinido. Regular -ar verbs end in -ó (él) and -aron (ellos): empezó, adelantó, ganó, adelantaron; -er/-ir verbs end in -ió: salió, llovió.
grammar.example: Después de un coche de seguridad, Verstappen adelantó a los dos y ganó.
grammar.title: Pretérito indefinido for finished events

grammar.body: "Era" (imperfect of ser) gives the situation, and "cuando" brings in the event that happened in it: he was third at the moment the car stopped (se detuvo).
grammar.example: Russell era tercero cuando su coche se detuvo a pocas vueltas del final.
grammar.title: Era + cuando + pretérito indefinido

paragraphs: El domingo 4 de octubre de 2026 llovió mucho en Sepang, en Malasia. La carrera de Fórmula 1 empezó unos noventa minutos tarde.
Max Verstappen salió primero con Red Bull, pero su salida fue lenta. Los dos pilotos de Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli y George Russell, lo adelantaron.
Después de un coche de seguridad, Verstappen adelantó a los dos y ganó. Fue su primera victoria de 2026.
Antonelli terminó segundo, a 2,3 segundos de Verstappen. Russell era tercero cuando su coche se detuvo a pocas vueltas del final. Lewis Hamilton terminó tercero con Ferrari.
Verstappen también ganó la última carrera en Sepang, en 2017. Antonelli sigue primero en el campeonato, con 84 puntos más que Russell. La próxima carrera es el domingo en Singapur.

grammar.body: "Tan fuerte que…" links a cause to its result: the rain was very heavy, and because of it Formula 1 had to wait.
grammar.example: El domingo 4 de octubre de 2026 la lluvia sobre Sepang era tan fuerte que la Fórmula 1 tuvo que esperar.
grammar.title: Tan + adjective + que

grammar.body: "Había perdido" (haber in the imperfect + participle) happened before "terminó": the pluscuamperfecto marks the earlier of two past events.
grammar.example: Lewis Hamilton, que había perdido muchos puestos en la salida, terminó tercero con Ferrari, detrás de Antonelli.
grammar.title: Pluscuamperfecto for the earlier event

grammar.body: "Sin embargo" (however) marks a contrast with the sentence before. Inside a sentence it stands between commas.
grammar.example: Después de un coche de seguridad, sin embargo, Verstappen los adelantó a los dos.
grammar.title: Sin embargo between commas

paragraphs: El domingo 4 de octubre de 2026 la lluvia sobre Sepang era tan fuerte que la Fórmula 1 tuvo que esperar. El Gran Premio de Baréin, trasladado este año a Malasia, empezó con unos noventa minutos de retraso.
Max Verstappen salió primero con Red Bull, pero fue lento en el circuito mojado. Los dos pilotos de Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli y George Russell, lo adelantaron enseguida.
Después de un coche de seguridad, sin embargo, Verstappen los adelantó a los dos. Ganó por 2,3 segundos: su primera victoria de 2026, y también la de su equipo.
Russell era tercero cuando su coche se detuvo de repente, a pocas vueltas del final. Lewis Hamilton, que había perdido muchos puestos en la salida, terminó tercero con Ferrari, detrás de Antonelli.
Antonelli tiene ahora 84 puntos de ventaja en el campeonato, y todavía quedan siete carreras. El próximo domingo se corre en Singapur. Verstappen ya había ganado la última carrera en Sepang, en 2017.

grammar.body: "Había sido trasladado" joins the pluscuamperfecto (había sido) and the passive (ser + participle): the move came before the race, and who moved it is not said. The subject (el Gran Premio de Baréin) comes after the verb, as it often does in a relative clause.
grammar.example: El domingo 4 de octubre de 2026, una lluvia torrencial hizo esperar a la Fórmula 1 en Sepang, adonde había sido trasladado este año el Gran Premio de Baréin.
grammar.title: Passive in the pluscuamperfecto

grammar.body: "Habiendo perdido muchos puestos" replaces "después de que había perdido…": the gerund of haber + participle is a compact, formal way to give the earlier action.
grammar.example: Antonelli terminó segundo, mientras que Lewis Hamilton, habiendo perdido muchos puestos en la salida, remontó hasta terminar tercero con Ferrari.
grammar.title: Compound gerund: habiendo + participle

grammar.body: "Una vez reagrupados los pilotos" means "once the drivers had been bunched up": the participle agrees with its noun and no conjugated verb is needed.
grammar.example: Una vez reagrupados los pilotos por un coche de seguridad, Verstappen adelantó a ambos y ya nadie pudo alcanzarlo.
grammar.title: Una vez + participle

paragraphs: El domingo 4 de octubre de 2026, una lluvia torrencial hizo esperar a la Fórmula 1 en Sepang, adonde había sido trasladado este año el Gran Premio de Baréin. La carrera comenzó con unos noventa minutos de retraso, sobre un circuito mojado.
Max Verstappen, primero en la parrilla con Red Bull, salió despacio, y los pilotos de Mercedes Kimi Antonelli y George Russell no tardaron en adelantarlo.

Duró poco. Una vez reagrupados los pilotos por un coche de seguridad, Verstappen adelantó a ambos y ya nadie pudo alcanzarlo. Terminó con 2,3 segundos de ventaja: su primera victoria de 2026, y también la de Red Bull.

Russell, que iba tercero, vio detenerse su monoplaza detrás de un coche de seguridad a pocas vueltas del final. Antonelli terminó segundo, mientras que Lewis Hamilton, habiendo perdido muchos puestos en la salida, remontó hasta terminar tercero con Ferrari.

Antonelli ha aumentado a 84 puntos su ventaja sobre Russell en el campeonato cuando quedan siete carreras, la próxima el domingo en Singapur. En cuanto a Verstappen, la última carrera de Fórmula 1 en Sepang, en 2017, también fue suya.

stories.summary: El domingo 4 de octubre de 2026 la lluvia hizo esperar a la Fórmula 1 una hora y media, y después Max Verstappen ganó en Sepang, el circuito donde había ganado por última vez nueve años antes.
stories.title: De vuelta en Sepang, Verstappen gana otra vez

grammar.body: This A1 story is told in the present: "comincia", "superano", "vince". Even 2017 is in the present here; the year shows when it happens.
grammar.example: Vince qui anche nel 2017.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: Italian usually leaves out "he", "she" or "it": the verb ending already shows who acts. "Vince" alone means "he wins"; "lui" is added only for contrast, as in "Poi lui supera…".
grammar.example: Vince per la Red Bull.
grammar.title: No subject pronoun needed

grammar.body: The object pronoun "lo" (him, it) stands before the verb, not after it as in English: "lo superano" = they pass him.
grammar.example: Due auto Mercedes lo superano.
grammar.title: "Lo" goes before the verb

paragraphs: È domenica 4 ottobre 2026. La Formula 1 è a Sepang, in Malesia. Piove forte. La gara comincia tardi.
Max Verstappen è primo alla partenza. Due auto Mercedes lo superano. Poi lui supera le due Mercedes. Vince per la Red Bull. È la sua prima vittoria di quest'anno.
Kimi Antonelli arriva secondo. George Russell è terzo, ma la sua auto si ferma. Così Lewis Hamilton arriva terzo per la Ferrari.
Verstappen conosce questa pista. Vince qui anche nel 2017. Domenica prossima la gara è a Singapore.

grammar.body: The spoken past is a present form of avere or essere plus a past participle: "ha vinto", "è partito". With essere the participle agrees with the subject: "la gara è cominciata", "l'auto si è fermata".
grammar.example: La gara di Formula 1 è cominciata con circa novanta minuti di ritardo.
grammar.title: Passato prossimo with avere and essere

grammar.body: "Era" (imperfect) describes the situation, while the passato prossimo tells what happened in it: he was third, and then the car stopped.
grammar.example: Russell era terzo, ma l'auto si è fermata a pochi giri dalla fine.
grammar.title: Era for the background

paragraphs: Domenica 4 ottobre 2026 ha piovuto forte a Sepang, in Malesia. La gara di Formula 1 è cominciata con circa novanta minuti di ritardo.
Max Verstappen è partito primo per la Red Bull. Ma la sua partenza è stata lenta. I due piloti Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli e George Russell, lo hanno superato.
Dopo una safety car Verstappen ha superato tutti e due ed è tornato primo. Ha vinto la gara, la sua prima vittoria del 2026.
Antonelli è arrivato secondo, a 2,3 secondi da Verstappen. Russell era terzo, ma l'auto si è fermata a pochi giri dalla fine. Lewis Hamilton ha preso il terzo posto per la Ferrari.
Verstappen ha vinto anche l'ultima gara a Sepang, nel 2017. Antonelli è ancora primo nel campionato, con 84 punti più di Russell. La prossima gara è domenica a Singapore.

grammar.body: "Così forte che…" links a cause to its result: the rain was very heavy, and because of it Formula 1 had to wait.
grammar.example: Domenica 4 ottobre 2026 la pioggia su Sepang era così forte che la Formula 1 ha dovuto aspettare.
grammar.title: Così + adjective + che

grammar.body: "Aveva perso" (imperfect of avere + past participle) happened before "è arrivato": the trapassato prossimo marks the earlier of two past events.
grammar.example: Lewis Hamilton, che alla partenza aveva perso molte posizioni, è arrivato terzo per la Ferrari dietro ad Antonelli.
grammar.title: Trapassato prossimo for the earlier event

grammar.body: With avere the participle normally does not change, but after the object pronouns lo, la, li, le it agrees with them: "li ha superati" (them, masculine plural), not "li ha superato".
grammar.example: Dopo una safety car, però, Verstappen li ha superati entrambi.
grammar.title: Participle agreement after lo, la, li, le

paragraphs: Domenica 4 ottobre 2026 la pioggia su Sepang era così forte che la Formula 1 ha dovuto aspettare. Il Gran Premio del Bahrein, spostato quest'anno in Malesia, è partito con circa novanta minuti di ritardo.
Max Verstappen è partito dalla pole position per la Red Bull, ma sulla pista bagnata è stato lento. I due piloti Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli e George Russell, lo hanno superato subito.
Dopo una safety car, però, Verstappen li ha superati entrambi. Ha vinto con 2,3 secondi di vantaggio: la prima vittoria del 2026 per lui e per la sua squadra.

Russell era terzo quando la sua auto si è fermata all'improvviso, a pochi giri dalla fine. Lewis Hamilton, che alla partenza aveva perso molte posizioni, è arrivato terzo per la Ferrari dietro ad Antonelli.
Ora Antonelli guida il campionato con 84 punti di vantaggio, a sette gare dalla fine. Domenica prossima si corre a Singapore. Verstappen aveva già vinto l'ultima gara a Sepang, nel 2017.

grammar.body: "Era stato spostato" combines the trapassato (era stato) with the passive (spostato): the move happened before the race, and who moved it is not important. The subject follows the verb here, which is common in Italian.
grammar.example: Domenica 4 ottobre 2026 una pioggia torrenziale ha fatto attendere la Formula 1 a Sepang, dove quest'anno era stato spostato il Gran Premio del Bahrein.
grammar.title: Trapassato prossimo in the passive

grammar.body: "Avendo perso molte posizioni" replaces "dopo che aveva perso molte posizioni": a compact, formal way to give the earlier action. The subject is the same as in the main clause.
grammar.example: Antonelli è arrivato secondo, mentre Lewis Hamilton, avendo perso molte posizioni alla partenza, è risalito al terzo posto per la Ferrari.
grammar.title: Gerundio composto: avendo + past participle

grammar.body: "Senza che" (without anyone …ing) always takes the subjunctive; after a past main verb it is the imperfect subjunctive: "riprendesse", from riprendere.
grammar.example: Dopo che una safety car aveva ricompattato il gruppo, Verstappen li ha superati entrambi, senza che nessuno lo riprendesse più.
grammar.title: Senza che + subjunctive

paragraphs: Domenica 4 ottobre 2026 una pioggia torrenziale ha fatto attendere la Formula 1 a Sepang, dove quest'anno era stato spostato il Gran Premio del Bahrein. La gara è cominciata con circa novanta minuti di ritardo, su pista bagnata.
Max Verstappen, in pole position per la Red Bull, è partito lentamente. I due piloti Mercedes, Kimi Antonelli e George Russell, lo hanno presto superato.

È durato poco. Dopo che una safety car aveva ricompattato il gruppo, Verstappen li ha superati entrambi, senza che nessuno lo riprendesse più. Ha vinto con 2,3 secondi di vantaggio: la sua prima vittoria del 2026, e la prima della Red Bull.

Russell, allora terzo, ha visto la sua auto fermarsi dietro una safety car a pochi giri dalla fine. Antonelli è arrivato secondo, mentre Lewis Hamilton, avendo perso molte posizioni alla partenza, è risalito al terzo posto per la Ferrari.

Il vantaggio di Antonelli su Russell in campionato è salito a 84 punti, a sette gare dalla fine. La prossima è domenica a Singapore. Quanto a Verstappen, anche l'ultima gara di Formula 1 a Sepang, nel 2017, era stata sua.

stories.summary: Domenica 4 ottobre 2026 la pioggia ha fatto aspettare la Formula 1 per un'ora e mezza, e poi Max Verstappen ha vinto a Sepang, la pista dove aveva vinto l'ultima volta nove anni prima.
stories.title: Di nuovo a Sepang, Verstappen vince ancora

grammar.body: This A1 story is told in the present, even for 1932: "is", "makes", "says". The year shows when it happens.
grammar.example: It is 1932 in Billund, Denmark.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: "Nobody" is singular, so the verb takes -s, and the sentence needs no "not": nobody has, nobody buys.
grammar.example: Nobody buys a house.
grammar.title: Nobody + verb with -s

paragraphs: It is 1932 in Billund, Denmark. Ole Kirk Christiansen is a carpenter. Nobody has money. Nobody buys a house.
So Ole makes wooden toys: a car, a yo-yo, later a duck. Children must play.
One day his son varnishes the ducks two times, not three. Ole says no. For a child, only the best is good enough. The son varnishes every duck again.
Ole's workshop burns two times. He builds it again. He names his company LEGO: "play well".

grammar.body: Regular verbs add -ed: ordered, burned, varnished, named. Irregular verbs change: make → made, send → sent, build → built, buy → bought.
grammar.example: Ole sent him back for the boxes.
grammar.title: Past simple: -ed and irregular forms

grammar.body: The past of "to be" is was (I, he, she, it) and were (you, we, they): "Ole was a carpenter", "times were hard".
grammar.example: Times were hard, and nobody ordered a house.
grammar.title: Was and were

paragraphs: In 1932 Ole Kirk Christiansen was a carpenter in Billund, a small village in Denmark. Times were hard, and nobody ordered a house.
So Ole made wooden toys: cars, yo-yos and, from 1935, a duck on wheels. Even poor parents bought something small for a child.
It was not easy. His workshop burned down in 1924 and again in 1942. Both times he built it again.
One day his son Godtfred sent ducks to the station with two coats of varnish, not three. Ole sent him back for the boxes. Godtfred varnished every duck again that night.
Ole's rule was simple: only the best is good enough. In 1934 he named his company LEGO, from the Danish for "play well".

grammar.body: "Was ordering" describes the situation at that time, not one finished action: was/were + verb-ing.
grammar.example: In 1932, in the Danish village of Billund, nobody was ordering a house.
grammar.title: Past continuous for the background

grammar.body: His words were "I have saved money". Reported after "told him that", the verb moves one step back, to the past perfect.
grammar.example: One day his son Godtfred told him that he had saved money.
grammar.title: Reported speech: told him that he had saved

grammar.body: "A duck that a child could pull": that introduces the clause saying which duck, and it is the object of pull.
grammar.example: So he began to make wooden toys: cars, yo-yos and, from 1935, a duck that a child could pull on a string.
grammar.title: Relative clause with that

paragraphs: In 1932, in the Danish village of Billund, nobody was ordering a house. Ole Kirk Christiansen, a carpenter, had a workshop and almost no work.
So he began to make wooden toys: cars, yo-yos and, from 1935, a duck that a child could pull on a string. Even poor families, he had noticed, found money for a child.
Nothing came easily. The workshop had burned down in 1924, and burned again in 1942. Each time he rebuilt it.

One day his son Godtfred told him that he had saved money. The ducks at the station had two coats of varnish, not three. Ole sent him to fetch the boxes, and Godtfred varnished every duck again that night.
"Only the best is good enough" became the company's rule. Ole had named it LEGO in 1934, from the Danish for "play well".

grammar.body: After "make" + person, the verb is the bare infinitive, without to: "made him fetch… and varnish". It means he had no choice.
grammar.example: Ole made him fetch the boxes from the station and varnish every duck again that night.
grammar.title: Make someone do something

grammar.body: Between commas, "which had burned down in 1924" adds information about the workshop without saying which one. "That" is not possible here.
grammar.example: The workshop, which had burned down in 1924, burned again in 1942; twice he rebuilt it.
grammar.title: Non-defining relative clause with which

grammar.body: "Hoping to save money" gives his reason in a compact, more formal way than "because he hoped to save money".
grammar.example: His son Godtfred, hoping to save money, once sent off a batch of ducks with two coats of varnish, not three.
grammar.title: Participle clause: hoping to save money

paragraphs: In 1932, in the Danish village of Billund, nobody was ordering a house, and the carpenter Ole Kirk Christiansen had a workshop and little work.
So he turned to wooden toys: cars, yo-yos and, from 1935, a duck pulled on a string. Families who could afford nothing else still found something for a child.
The workshop, which had burned down in 1924, burned again in 1942; twice he rebuilt it.
His son Godtfred, hoping to save money, once sent off a batch of ducks with two coats of varnish, not three. Ole made him fetch the boxes from the station and varnish every duck again that night.

"Only the best is good enough" became the motto of the company he had named LEGO in 1934, from the Danish for "play well". Its plastic brick was patented on 28 January 1958, six weeks before Ole died on 11 March. A toy is no small thing to the child who gets it.

stories.summary: In 1932 a Danish village carpenter with no houses to build began to make wooden toys, and one evening he sent his son back to the station to varnish every duck again.
stories.title: The Wooden Duck

grammar.body: This A1 story is told in the present, even for 1932: "est", "fabrique", "répond". "Nous sommes en 1932" is the French way to say "it is 1932".
grammar.example: Nous sommes en 1932 à Billund, au Danemark.
grammar.title: Present tense for a story

grammar.body: French says what someone is without an article: "Ole est charpentier", not "un charpentier".
grammar.example: Ole Kirk Christiansen est charpentier.
grammar.title: No article before a profession

grammar.body: After a negative, "un", "une" and "des" become "de": il achète une maison, but personne n'achète de maison.
grammar.example: Personne n'achète de maison.
grammar.title: De after a negative

paragraphs: Nous sommes en 1932 à Billund, au Danemark. Ole Kirk Christiansen est charpentier. Personne n'a d'argent. Personne n'achète de maison.
Alors Ole fabrique des jouets en bois. Il fabrique une voiture, un yo-yo, plus tard un canard. Les enfants doivent jouer.
Un jour, son fils vernit les canards deux fois, pas trois. Ole répond non. Pour un enfant, seul le meilleur est assez bon. Le fils vernit encore une fois tous les canards.
L'atelier d'Ole brûle deux fois. Ole reconstruit l'atelier. Il appelle son entreprise LEGO : « joue bien ».

grammar.body: The spoken past is avoir in the present plus a past participle: a fabriqué, a brûlé, a envoyé. Verbs in -er give -é; a verb in -ir like revernir gives -i: a reverni.
grammar.example: Un jour, son fils Godtfred a envoyé des canards à la gare.
grammar.title: Passé composé with avoir

grammar.body: The imparfait of être and avoir describes how things were, not one event: "Ole était charpentier", "ils avaient deux couches".
grammar.example: Ils avaient deux couches de vernis, pas trois.
grammar.title: Était and avaient for the background

grammar.body: "L'" stands for "l'atelier" and goes before avoir, not after the verb: il l'a reconstruit = he rebuilt it.
grammar.example: Les deux fois, il l'a reconstruit.
grammar.title: Object pronoun before the auxiliary

paragraphs: En 1932, Ole Kirk Christiansen était charpentier à Billund, un petit village du Danemark. Les temps étaient durs. Cette année-là, personne n'a commandé de maison.
Alors Ole a fabriqué des jouets en bois : des voitures, des yo-yos et, dès 1935, un canard à roulettes. Même les parents pauvres ont acheté une petite chose pour un enfant.
Ce n'était pas facile. Son atelier a brûlé en 1924, puis encore en 1942. Les deux fois, il l'a reconstruit.
Un jour, son fils Godtfred a envoyé des canards à la gare. Ils avaient deux couches de vernis, pas trois. Ole l'a renvoyé récupérer les boîtes. Cette nuit-là, Godtfred a reverni chaque canard.
La règle d'Ole était simple : seul le meilleur est assez bon. En 1934, il a appelé son entreprise LEGO, des mots danois pour « joue bien ».

grammar.body: "Commandait" describes the situation at that time, not one finished action; the passé composé (a commencé, a ajouté) then tells what happened.
grammar.example: En 1932, dans le village danois de Billund, personne ne commandait de maison.
grammar.title: Imparfait for the background

grammar.body: His words were "j'ai économisé de l'argent". Reported after "lui a dit que", the verb moves one step back: il avait économisé.
grammar.example: Un jour, son fils Godtfred lui a dit qu'il avait économisé de l'argent.
grammar.title: Reported speech with the plus-que-parfait

grammar.body: "Que" is the object of the clause it opens: the child pulls the duck. Before a vowel it shortens to "qu'".
grammar.example: Dès 1935, il a ajouté un canard qu'un enfant pouvait tirer avec une ficelle.
grammar.title: Relative pronoun que (qu')

paragraphs: En 1932, dans le village danois de Billund, personne ne commandait de maison. Ole Kirk Christiansen, charpentier, avait un atelier et presque pas de travail.
